steps: Lie on your back with both legs straight, then lift one leg so the hip and knee are both bent to 90 degrees, holding behind the thigh with both hands.
Keeping the thigh still, slowly straighten the knee and pull your toes toward you until you feel a stretch in the back of the thigh and calf.
Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly, then bend the knee and switch legs.
Keep the other leg and your lower back flat on the floor; you don't need to fully straighten the knee.
fedb:90_90_Hamstring.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Old steps described 10–20 reps; rewritten as a hold to match mode 'time' (it can also be done as slow extend-and-bend reps). One leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Lie face down on your forearms, bend one knee and bring that leg out to the side so the inner thigh rests on a foam roller lying roughly parallel to your body.
Start just above the knee and slowly roll toward the groin by shifting your body sideways an inch or two at a time, using your forearms and the other leg to control the pressure.
Expect firm, achy pressure along the inner thigh; on a tender spot, pause and breathe slowly for 20–30 seconds until it eases – about 5–7 out of 10, never sharp pain.
Cover the whole inner thigh for about a minute, then switch legs.
Don't roll fast, and keep the roller off the knee joint and the groin crease; take more weight on your arms or use a softer roller if it's too intense.

references.title: Foam Roll Adductors
Foam Roller Techniques and Tips for the Lower Body

steps: Lie on your back with both legs raised straight toward the ceiling while a partner kneels at your feet and holds your ankles.
Open your legs out to the sides as far as is comfortable; you should feel a stretch along your inner thighs.
Press your legs inward against your partner's hands for about 10 seconds while they hold them still, breathing normally.
Relax and breathe out as your partner gently eases your legs a little wider, then hold for 20–30 seconds.
Tell your partner straight away when the stretch is enough; there should be no bouncing or sudden pushing.
fedb:Adductor_Groin.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Partner-assisted contract-relax (PNF) stretch; it needs a partner.

steps: Start on your hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips, padding your knees if needed.
Lift one foot toward your buttock and reach back with the opposite hand (more stable) to hold the foot or ankle.
Gently draw the heel in and ease your hips forward and down until you feel a stretch along the front of the thigh and hip.
Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly, then switch sides.
Brace your core so your lower back doesn't sag; if you can't reach the foot, loop a towel or strap around it.
fedb:All_Fours_Quad_Stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. One leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Stand beside a wall or rack and hold it lightly for balance.
Shift your weight onto one leg and lift the other foot a couple of inches off the floor.
Slowly draw big circles with your big toe, moving only at the ankle; you should feel the ankle and calf loosen.
Breathe normally and circle for about 15–20 seconds in each direction, then switch feet.
Keep the knee and shin still; sit on a chair instead if balancing is hard.
fedb:Ankle_Circles.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. One foot at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Cross one ankle over the opposite thigh just above the knee and let the crossed knee fall open.
Hold behind the thigh of the bottom leg and gently pull both legs toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the glute and outer hip of the crossed leg.
Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor and hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly, then switch sides.
If you can't reach the thigh comfortably, keep the bottom foot on the floor or use a strap.
fedb:Ankle_On_The_Knee.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. This is the lying figure-four stretch; one side at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Sit on the floor or a chair with your knees bent and feet flat, holding a handheld muscle roller (stick) or rolling pin.
Place the roller on the front-outer part of your shin, just to the outside of the shinbone, below the knee.
Roll slowly down to just above the ankle and back with moderate pressure; you should feel it in the muscle beside the shin, not the bone.
Pause on any tender spot for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly, then switch legs.
Keep off the bony front edge of the shin and ease the pressure if it feels sharp.
fedb:Anterior_Tibialis-SMR.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Tibialis anterior sits at the front of the shin, but the entry's primary muscle is 'calves'. One leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and raise both arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, palms down.
Make small, controlled circles about a foot across with both arms, growing them a little if comfortable.
You should feel your shoulders and upper back warm up; keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
Breathe normally and circle forward for 10–15 seconds, then reverse for the same time.
Keep your arms straight and core braced; if your arms tire, lower them briefly and restart.
fedb:Arm_Circles.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Current steps were already correct.

steps: Sit tall on the floor or a bench with a partner kneeling or standing behind you.
Lace your fingers behind your head and draw your elbows back as far as is comfortable, then have your partner hold your elbows.
Press your elbows forward against your partner's hands for about 10 seconds while they keep them still.
Relax and breathe out as your partner gently eases your elbows back, then hold for 20–30 seconds; feel it across your chest and front shoulders.
Don't pull on your head or neck, and tell your partner straight away when the stretch is enough.
fedb:Behind_Head_Chest_Stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Partner-assisted contract-relax (PNF) stretch; it needs a partner. Fixed the typo 'behind your hand' in the old steps.

steps: Lie on your side or front with your arm out to the side and a foam roller under the outer front of your upper arm, just above the elbow.
Support yourself with your other hand and feet, then shift your weight onto the arm and roll slowly from just above the elbow toward the shoulder.
You should feel pressure along the front and outer side of the upper arm; pause on tender spots.
Breathe slowly and hold each tender spot for 20 to 30 seconds for the set time, then switch arms.
Keep the roller off the elbow joint; a smaller ball pressed against a table gives more control if the roller feels awkward.
fedb:Brachialis-SMR.note: No reputable page found for rolling the brachialis; it lies deep under the biceps, so a roller mostly reaches the biceps/outer upper arm. One arm at a time, so perSide should be true. Web search limit was reached.

steps: Stand facing a wall a little more than an arm's length away, with your feet hip-width apart and toes pointing at the wall.
Lean forward and rest your forearms on the wall at about shoulder height, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Keep your legs straight and your heels pressed into the floor; you should feel the stretch in both calves.
Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly.
Step your feet further back for a stronger stretch or closer to ease it, and don't let your hips bend or your heels lift.
fedb:Calf_Stretch_Elbows_Against_Wall.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Both calves at once.

steps: Stand facing a wall and place both hands on it at shoulder height.
Step one foot back about a stride, keeping the back leg straight with the heel down and toes forward, and bend the front knee.
Lean your hips toward the wall, keeping a straight line from back heel to head, until you feel a stretch in the calf of the back leg.
Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly, then switch legs.
Don't let the back heel lift or the foot turn out; bend the back knee slightly to stretch the lower calf.
fedb:Calf_Stretch_Hands_Against_Wall.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Staggered stance stretches one calf at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Sit with your legs straight, a foam roller under one calf and hands on the floor behind you; cross the other leg on top for more pressure.
Press through your hands to lift your hips and roll slowly from just below the knee to just above the ankle.
Feel the pressure in your calf muscle, and turn the leg slightly in and out to reach the inner and outer edges.
Breathe steadily and pause on tender spots for 20 to 30 seconds for the set time, then switch legs.
Do not roll over the back of the knee or the ankle bone, and keep the pressure at a tolerable level.

references.title: Foam Roll Calves
Foam Roller Techniques and Tips for the Lower Body

fedb:Calves-SMR.note: Rolled one leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Start on your hands and knees with wrists under shoulders, knees under hips and your back flat.
As you breathe out, pull your belly button toward your spine and round your back up toward the ceiling, letting your head and tailbone drop.
Press the floor away with your hands so you feel the stretch between your shoulder blades and along your back.
Hold for 15–30 seconds while breathing slowly, then return to a flat back.
Pad your knees if they're sensitive, and let your head hang rather than forcing your chin into your chest.
fedb:Cat_Stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. This is the yoga Cat pose (Marjaryasana).

steps: Sit tall near the front of a sturdy chair and hold the sides of the seat.
Straighten one knee to lift that leg out in front of you, pulling your toes back so you feel the back of the thigh and calf.
Slowly sweep the straight leg out to the side as far as is comfortable, pause to feel the inner thigh, then bring it back to the middle and lower it.
Breathe steadily and repeat smoothly for about 20–30 seconds, then switch legs.
Keep your back upright without leaning away from the moving leg, and lift the leg lower if your hip starts to cramp.
fedb:Chair_Leg_Extended_Stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. This is a slow dynamic movement filed under mode 'time'. One leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Sit tall on a sturdy chair with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Hold the side of the seat with one hand and raise the other arm straight overhead.
Lean your upper body sideways away from the raised arm, reaching up and over, until you feel a stretch along that side of your back and ribs.
Hold for 10–30 seconds while breathing into your side ribs, then come back up and switch sides.
Keep both sitting bones on the seat and bend straight to the side rather than leaning forward.
fedb:Chair_Lower_Back_Stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. This is really a seated side bend (lats and side of the lower back). One side at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Sit on the front edge of a sturdy chair with your feet flat, then reach both hands behind you and grip the chair back.
Straighten your arms and lift your chest, drawing your shoulder blades together.
Gently lean your upper body forward with a straight back until you feel a stretch across the front of your shoulders, chest and upper arms.
Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears and ease off if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.
fedb:Chair_Upper_Body_Stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Old steps were vague about hand position; this assumes hands behind you on the chair back, which matches the listed muscles.

steps: Stand tall with your feet together or hip-width apart, holding a broomstick or light bar in front of your thighs with a wide overhand grip.
Keeping your arms straight, slowly raise the stick up overhead.
Carry it back behind your head only as far as is comfortable, until you feel a stretch across your chest and the front of your shoulders.
Hold for 15–30 seconds while breathing slowly, then bring the stick back over to the front.
Widen your grip if you have to bend your elbows or arch your lower back to get the stick back.
fedb:Chest_And_Front_Of_Shoulder_Stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Old steps had no hold or finish; added.

steps: Kneel on all fours beside a stability ball, with the ball level with one shoulder.
Place that forearm on top of the ball with your arm out to the side and the elbow bent at about 90 degrees, level with your shoulder.
Keeping the forearm on the ball, slowly lower your chest toward the floor until you feel a stretch across that side of your chest and front shoulder.
Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly, then switch arms.
Only sink as far as is comfortable, and stop if you feel pinching in the shoulder.
fedb:Chest_Stretch_on_Stability_Ball.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. One arm at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Kneel on the floor with your big toes together and knees about hip-width apart or wider, then sit your hips back toward your heels.
Walk your hands forward and fold your chest down toward your thighs, resting your forehead on the floor.
Leave your arms stretched forward or rest them alongside your body, palms up, and feel a gentle stretch through your back and hips.
Breathe slowly into your back and hold for 30–60 seconds.
Put a cushion under your hips or a block under your forehead if they don't reach, and skip the pose if it hurts your knees.
fedb:Childs_Pose.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. This is Balasana; current steps were correct apart from missing the knee setup.

steps: Sit tall on the floor or a chair with your shoulders relaxed.
Lace your fingers and rest your hands on the back of your head, elbows pointing forward.
Let the weight of your hands gently draw your chin toward your chest until you feel a stretch along the back of your neck and upper back.
Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly.
Don't pull hard on your head; let your arms rest, and stop if you feel tingling or pain down your arms.
fedb:Chin_To_Chest_Stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out.

steps: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms crossed over your chest or your hands together in front.
Step one foot back into a reverse lunge, bending both knees until the back knee is just above the floor.
As you lower, rotate your chest and shoulders toward the side of the front leg, feeling a twist through your back and a stretch at the front of the back hip.
Turn back to centre, step up to standing and repeat on the other side, alternating steadily for 30–45 seconds and breathing out on each twist.
Turn from your upper body and keep the front knee pointing straight over your toes; take a shorter step if you lose balance.
fedb:Crossover_Reverse_Lunge.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. The name is ambiguous: the old steps say to rotate 'across the front leg', read here as twisting toward the front-leg side. It is a dynamic alternating move filed under mode 'time'.

steps: Sit tall on the floor with both legs straight in front of you.
Bend your right knee and cross it over your left leg, placing the right foot flat on the floor outside the left knee.
Put your right hand on the floor behind you and hook your left arm around the right knee.
Breathe in to sit tall, then breathe out and turn to the right, feeling the stretch in your lower back and outer right hip; hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.
Keep both sitting bones down and your spine long rather than slumped; sit on a folded towel if your back rounds.
fedb:Dancers_Stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. This is a seated spinal twist (like a simple Half Lord of the Fishes). It works one side at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft and arms hanging straight in front of your thighs.
Keeping your elbows straight, swing both arms forward and up overhead, then let them swing back down past your hips in a smooth arc.
Start with small swings and make each a little bigger until your arms reach fully overhead, feeling your lats, shoulders and upper back loosen.
Breathe in as your arms rise and out as they drop, keeping a steady rhythm for the set time (about 10-15 swings).
Avoid arching your lower back or shrugging as the arms go up; keep your ribs down and the swing controlled rather than flung.
fedb:Dynamic_Back_Stretch.note: No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, palms facing each other.
Keeping your arms straight and level, swing them open out to the sides and back as far as is comfortable, then bring them back together like a big clap.
Feel a stretch across your chest and the front of your shoulders on each opening swing, with your shoulder blades squeezing together.
Breathe in as you open and out as you close, starting slowly and building speed and range for the set time (about 10-15 swings).
Don't arch your lower back or fling your arms past a comfortable range; a slight bend in the elbows eases strain on the shoulders.
fedb:Dynamic_Chest_Stretch.note: No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Sit or stand tall with feet slightly apart and place your fingertips on the tops of your shoulders, elbows pointing out to the sides at shoulder height.
Slowly draw large circles with your elbows, moving them forward, up, back and down, then reverse direction.
Feel the shoulder joints and the muscles around your shoulder blades and upper back loosening as you circle.
Breathe out as you start each circle and in as you finish it, continuing smoothly for the set time, about 10 circles each way.
Keep your neck relaxed and avoid shrugging; make the circles smaller if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.
fedb:Elbow_Circles.note: No preferred-site page found; only fitness-app pages describe this exact drill.

steps: Stand or sit tall and place both hands on your lower back, fingertips pointing down toward your belt line and elbows out to the sides.
Gently draw your elbows back toward each other, squeezing your shoulder blades together and lifting your chest.
Feel the stretch spread across the front of your chest and shoulders.
Breathe deeply and hold for the set time (about 15-30 seconds), easing the elbows a little further back as you breathe out.
Keep your chin level and avoid arching your lower back or pushing your hips forward; only move as far as feels comfortable.

references.title: Pulmonary Rehabilitation after COVID-19 related illness (exercise sheet)
Active Against Cancer exercise diary (Harrogate and District NHS Foundation Trust)

fedb:Elbows_Back.note: References are NHS trust patient PDFs with illustrations; page titles cleaned up from the search listing.

steps: Sit on a chair with shoes off and place one foot on a foot roller, massage ball or small length of pipe under the arch.
Press down with comfortable pressure and slowly roll from your heel to the ball of your foot and back, pausing on tender spots.
You should feel firm pressure and release along the sole and arch, not sharp pain.
Breathe steadily and keep rolling for the set time (about 30-60 seconds), then switch feet.
Stand and lean onto the foot only if you want more pressure; a frozen water bottle works well too and doubles as an ice massage.

references.title: Plantar fasciitis - Diagnosis and treatment - Mayo Clinic

fedb:Foot-SMR.note: Done one foot at a time, so perSide should be true. Mayo page mentions rolling a ball or frozen bottle under the foot but is not a dedicated how-to. Primary muscle 'calves' is a stretch; it mainly targets the sole/plantar fascia.

steps: Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width, hands lightly behind your head, and squat down with your chest up and eyes forward.
Drive through your legs to jump forward a short distance, staying low rather than jumping high.
Land softly through the balls and middle of your feet, bending your knees and hips to sink straight back into the squat, then hop again.
You'll feel it in your quads, glutes and calves; breathe out on each jump and keep a steady rhythm for the set time (about 5-10 hops).
Keep your knees tracking over your toes and never land stiff-legged; drop your hands for balance or do squat jumps in place to make it easier.

references.title: Frog jumps (Jumping forward, like a frog)

fedb:Frog_Hops.note: This is a plyometric drill rather than a stretch; mode 'reps' may fit better than 'time'.

steps: Stand side-on to a wall, chair or rack and hold it with your near hand, standing tall on the inside leg.
Keeping the outside leg fairly straight, swing it forward and up, then let it swing back behind you like a pendulum.
Start small and gradually swing higher, feeling the hamstrings stretch on the forward swing and the front of the hip on the back swing.
Breathe steadily and swing for the set time (about 10-15 swings), then turn around and switch legs.
Keep your torso upright and avoid rounding your back or kicking hard; only swing as high as you can control.
fedb:Front_Leg_Raises.note: Standing front-to-back leg swings; done one leg at a time, so perSide should be true. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent out to the sides and the soles of your feet together, then lace your fingers lightly behind your head.
Slowly round forward, bringing your elbows down toward the insides of your thighs or knees.
Feel the stretch in your inner thighs and along your lower and middle back.
Breathe out as you curl down, pause briefly, then breathe in as you sit back up tall; repeat smoothly for the set time (about 10-20 reps).
Don't pull on your neck with your hands; if your hips are tight, slide your feet farther away or hold your ankles instead.
fedb:Groin_and_Back_Stretch.note: Seated butterfly with a forward curl; source describes 10-20 reps, so mode 'reps' may fit better. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Start in a high push-up position with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Hop both feet forward to land wide, just outside your hands, and sink your hips low with your chest and head up.
Feel the stretch in your inner thighs and hips at the bottom, then hop or step your feet back to the push-up position.
Breathe out as your feet come in and keep a steady rhythm for the set time (about 10-20 reps).
Don't let your hips sag or pike in the plank; for an easier version, step one foot at a time up beside the same-side hand, alternating.
fedb:Groiners.note: Ambiguous name: 'groiner' also commonly means an alternating step of one foot outside the hand (spider-man lunge). Steps follow the source's two-foot jump, with feet landing wide. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Sit on the floor with your legs straight and a foam roller under the back of your thighs, hands on the floor behind you.
Press through your hands to lift your hips and shift your weight onto one leg; cross the other leg on top for more pressure.
Roll slowly from just below your hip to just above the back of the knee, feeling pressure in the hamstring, and turn the leg slightly in and out.
Breathe steadily and pause on tender spots for 20 to 30 seconds for the set time, then switch legs.
Relax the leg being rolled and keep the roller off the back of the knee; keep both legs on the roller for less pressure.

references.title: Foam Rolling Techniques: A 4 Step Formula
Foam Roller Techniques and Tips for the Lower Body

fedb:Hamstring-SMR.note: Rolled one leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Lie on your back with one leg flat on the floor and loop a strap, towel or band around the ball of the other foot.
Raise the looped leg toward the ceiling, keeping the knee as straight as is comfortable, until your hip is bent about 90 degrees.
Gently pull on the strap to draw the leg toward you until you feel a stretch along the back of your thigh and into the calf.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time (about 20-30 seconds), relaxing a little deeper as you breathe out, then switch legs.
Keep your hips and the resting leg on the floor and don't yank the strap; bend the resting knee, foot flat, if your lower back strains.
fedb:Hamstring_Stretch.note: Supine strap hamstring stretch done one leg at a time, so perSide should be true. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Start on your hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips, with a flat back.
Lift one bent knee slightly off the floor and slowly draw a big circle with it, moving forward, out to the side, back and in.
Feel the work around the hip and buttock of the moving leg and a gentle stretch through the inner and outer hip.
Breathe steadily, make several slow circles one way and then reverse for the set time, then switch legs.
Keep your hips and shoulders level and don't let your lower back sag or twist; make the circles smaller if you lose control.
fedb:Hip_Circles_prone.note: Quadruped hip circles done one leg at a time, so perSide should be true. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Place an exercise ball on the floor in front of you and stand with your feet wider than hip-width, toes slightly out, so the ball sits between your knees.
Wrap your arms around the ball and, holding it for balance, slowly lower your hips into a deep squat toward the floor.
Keep your feet flat and knees over your ankles, and let your back round gently over the ball to feel a stretch in your lower back, glutes and calves.
Breathe slowly and relax into the hold for the set time.
Keep a firm hold so the ball can't roll away and tip you back; keep your hips higher or sit on a low block if your heels lift.
fedb:Hug_A_Ball.note: Source text is unclear (starts 'seat yourself on the floor' then 'lower your hips'); interpreted as a deep supported squat hugging a ball. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Bring both knees up toward your chest and hold the backs of your thighs, just under the knees, with your hands.
Gently draw your knees toward your shoulders until you feel a stretch in your lower back and buttocks, keeping your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time, letting your lower back relax a little more each time you breathe out.
Hold under the knees rather than over the shins to spare your knees, and bring one knee in at a time if both feels like too much.
fedb:Hug_Knees_To_Chest.note: No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Lie on your back with both legs straight and loop a strap or band around one foot, holding the ends in the opposite hand.
Raise the strapped leg, then guide it across your body toward the opposite side, keeping the knee straight and the foot off the floor.
Gently pull the strap to draw the toes up and the leg further across until you feel a stretch along the outside of your hip and thigh.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time (about 20-30 seconds), then bring the leg back to center and switch sides.
Keep the opposite shoulder on the floor and only cross as far as your hips stay comfortable; soften the knee if the back of the thigh pulls too much.
fedb:IT_Band_and_Glute_Stretch.note: Done one leg at a time, so perSide should be true. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Lie on your side propped on your forearm with a foam roller under the outer thigh of your bottom leg, top leg crossed in front with its foot on the floor.
Use your forearm and top foot to control the pressure and roll slowly from just below the hip to just above the knee.
Feel pressure along the outside of your thigh, and tilt slightly forward or back to reach the muscle beside the band.
Breathe slowly and pause on tender spots for 20 to 30 seconds for the set time, then switch legs.
This area is often very sensitive, so push more weight through your top foot to ease off, and do not roll over the hip bone or knee.

references.title: Foam Roller Techniques and Tips for the Lower Body
IT Band Self-Care: Reduce Pain & Improve Mobility

fedb:Iliotibial_Tract-SMR.note: Rolled one leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, hinge at your hips and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet, bending your knees only as much as you need.
Walk your hands forward one at a time until you reach a high plank with your shoulders over your wrists and your body in a straight line.
Keep your hands still and walk your feet in with small steps toward them, legs as straight as you can, to feel the stretch in your hamstrings and calves.
Breathe steadily and repeat the walk-out and walk-in for the set time (about 5-8 reps).
Brace your core so your hips don't sag in the plank, and bend your knees as much as needed to reach the floor.
fedb:Inchworm.note: Dynamic drill; mode 'reps' may fit better than 'time'. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Lie on your back with both legs straight and loop a strap, belt or band around one foot, holding the ends in the hand on that side.
Raise the strapped leg toward the ceiling, then slowly lower it out to the side as far as is comfortable, keeping the knee straight.
Use the strap to gently guide the leg until you feel a stretch along your inner thigh and the back of the thigh.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time (about 20-30 seconds), then bring the leg back to center and switch sides.
Keep the opposite hip pressed to the floor so your pelvis doesn't roll, and rest the outer thigh on a cushion if it's too intense.
fedb:Intermediate_Groin_Stretch.note: Done one leg at a time, so perSide should be true. Primary muscle listed as hamstrings; the main target is the adductors (groin). No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Lie face down with your forehead on the floor or a folded towel and loop a strap or band around one ankle, holding the ends over your shoulder with both hands.
Bend that knee to bring your heel toward your buttock, then gently pull the strap so the knee and thigh lift slightly off the floor.
Feel the stretch along the front of the thigh and the front of the hip.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time (about 20-30 seconds), then lower the leg and switch sides.
Keep both hips pressed into the floor and avoid arching your lower back; just bending the knee without lifting the thigh is an easier option.
fedb:Intermediate_Hip_Flexor_and_Quad_St.note: Done one leg at a time, so perSide should be true. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Lie face down with your legs straight and your arms out to the sides in a T, palms pressed to the floor.
Bend one knee and swing that leg up and across behind your body, reaching the foot toward the floor near your opposite hand.
Feel the stretch across the front of the hip and thigh, the abs and the lower back as your hips rotate.
Return to the start with control and repeat with the other leg, breathing out as you reach, alternating for the set time (about 10 per side).
Keep both shoulders and your chest on the floor, reach only as far as is comfortable, and move smoothly instead of flinging the leg.
fedb:Iron_Crosses_stretch.note: Also commonly called the scorpion stretch; alternates legs. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Lie on your back with your right leg straight, then bend your left knee and draw it up toward your chest.
Guide the left knee across your body toward the floor on your right, holding it with your right hand, and rest your left arm out to the side.
Turn your head to the left and keep both shoulders down to feel a stretch in your left buttock, outer hip and lower back.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time, letting the knee sink a little more as you breathe out, then switch sides.
The knee doesn't need to reach the floor; rest it on a cushion if you're tight, and keep the opposite shoulder from lifting.
fedb:Knee_Across_The_Body.note: Supine knee-across twist; the source says to switch sides, so perSide should be true. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Stand with your feet together, bend your knees slightly and rest your hands lightly on your knees or hips.
Keeping your feet flat, move both knees together in slow circles: forward, to one side, back and to the other side.
Feel gentle movement and warmth through your knees, ankles and the muscles around them.
Breathe normally and do several circles in one direction, then reverse, continuing for the set time.
Keep the circles small and smooth, avoid snapping the knees straight as they pass back, and stop if you feel pain inside the knee.
fedb:Knee_Circles.note: No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Kneel on a mat on all fours and place your palms flat on the floor, turning your hands so your fingers point back toward your knees.
Keeping your palms flat and elbows straight, slowly lean your hips back toward your heels.
Stop when you feel a stretch along the inside of your forearms and wrists.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time (about 20-30 seconds).
Lean back only a little at first; keep your hands closer to your knees or turn the fingers out to the sides to make it gentler.
fedb:Kneeling_Forearm_Stretch.note: No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Kneel on a mat, then step one foot forward, flat, with that knee bent about 90 degrees, resting the back knee and top of that foot on the floor.
Tuck your tailbone slightly and squeeze the glute of the back leg, then shift your hips forward until you feel a stretch at the front of that hip and thigh.
Keep your torso upright with hands on your front thigh or hips, and your front knee roughly over your ankle.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time (about 20-30 seconds), then switch legs.
Don't arch your lower back to get deeper, and put a folded towel or pad under the back knee for comfort.
fedb:Kneeling_Hip_Flexor.note: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch; the source says to repeat on the other side, so perSide should be true. Secondary muscle duplicates primary (quadriceps). No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Lie on your side with a foam roller just below and behind your armpit, bottom arm stretched overhead with the thumb up, and knees bent.
Use your feet to shift your weight onto the roller and roll slowly from the armpit down toward the middle of your ribs.
Feel pressure along the side of your upper back; rock slightly forward and back to find tender spots.
Breathe slowly and hold tender spots for 20 to 30 seconds for the set time, then switch sides.
Stay on the muscle behind the armpit rather than the ribs or shoulder joint, and take more weight through your feet if it is too intense.

references.title: Foam Roll Latissimus Dorsi

fedb:Latissimus_Dorsi-SMR.note: Rolled one side at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Lie on your back, bend one knee and put that foot flat on the floor to support your lower back.
Lift the other leg toward the ceiling and hold the back of your thigh or calf with both hands, or loop a strap around the foot.
Slowly straighten the knee so the sole faces the ceiling, then gently draw the leg toward your face until you feel a stretch along the back of the thigh.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time, then switch legs.
It's fine if the knee stays slightly bent; don't pull on the knee joint itself or lift your hips and head off the floor.
fedb:Leg-Up_Hamstring_Stretch.note: Done one leg at a time, so perSide should be true. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Kneel on a mat with your knees hip-width apart and the tops of your feet on the floor, or tuck your toes to raise your heels.
Place your hands on your lower back, then reach back one hand at a time to hold your heels.
Press your hips forward, lift your chest and gently let your head go back to look at the ceiling, arching your back.
Feel the stretch along the fronts of your thighs and hips, your abs and chest, and breathe steadily as you hold for the set time.
Keep your hips over your knees and don't crunch your neck; keep your hands on your lower back or tuck your toes to make it easier.
fedb:Looking_At_Ceiling.note: Essentially Camel Pose (Ustrasana). No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat, then lean back so a foam roller sits across your lower back above your pelvis, arms crossed over your chest.
Lift your hips slightly and lean to one side so the pressure is on the muscles beside your spine rather than on the spine itself.
Roll gently in small movements between the bottom of your ribs and the top of your pelvis, feeling broad pressure in the low-back muscles.
Breathe slowly and pause on tight spots for 10 to 30 seconds, then shift to the other side for the rest of the set time.
Keep the pressure light and stop if you feel sharp or nerve pain; rolling your glutes and mid-back is a safer option.
fedb:Lower_Back-SMR.note: Several coaching sources (e.g. ACE) advise against rolling directly on the lumbar spine; steps keep it gentle and off the spine. Consider replacing with a ball beside the spine or removing. Done one side at a time, so perSide true. Web search limit was reached.

steps: Lie face down with your legs straight and your arms out to the sides, forehead resting on the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and use your lower back muscles to slowly lift your chest a few inches off the floor, without pushing with your arms.
Keep your neck long with your eyes on the floor just ahead, and feel the work along your lower back.
Breathe in as you lift, pause briefly, then breathe out as you lower; repeat smoothly for the set time (about 10-20 reps).
Lift only as high as is comfortable without pinching in your lower back; keep your arms by your sides for an easier version.
fedb:Lower_Back_Curl.note: Prone back extension; primary muscle should be lower back (erector spinae), not abdominals. Source describes reps, so mode 'reps' may fit better. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Lie on your back with the soles of your feet together and knees falling out to the sides, while a partner kneels at your feet holding your inner knees.
Gently squeeze your knees together against your partner's hands for about 10 seconds while they keep them still.
Relax and breathe out as your partner slowly presses your knees toward the floor, deepening the stretch in your inner thighs.
Hold the new position for the set time, breathing slowly, and repeat the squeeze-and-relax cycle 2-3 times.
Tell your partner clearly when the stretch is enough; without a partner, just let gravity open your knees or press them gently with your own hands.
fedb:Lying_Bent_Leg_Groin.note: Partner-assisted (PNF contract-relax) butterfly stretch. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Lie on your back with both legs straight, then bend one knee and bring it across your body toward the floor on the opposite side, keeping both shoulders down.
Your partner kneels beside you, one hand holding your shoulder on the floor and the other on the outside of your crossed knee.
Gently press the knee up into your partner's hand for about 6–10 seconds while they stop it moving; you should feel your outer hip and buttock working.
Relax and breathe out as your partner eases the knee a little closer to the floor, hold 15–30 seconds, then repeat on the other side.
Tell your partner to stop at mild tension, never pain; without a partner, guide the knee down with your own opposite hand.

references.title: Iliotibial (IT) Band: Syndrome, Strength, Stretches, and Prevention

fedb:Lying_Crossover.note: Partner-assisted PNF (contract-relax) version, as in the images; the reference shows the solo lying knee-across-body stretch.

steps: Lie on your back with your partner kneeling beside you, then lift one bent leg and turn it out so your shin lies across your body above the opposite hip.
Your partner holds your knee and ankle while you gently push the leg toward them for about 6–10 seconds without it moving.
Relax and breathe out as your partner eases your knee and ankle toward your chest; feel it deep in the buttock and outer hip of the bent leg.
Hold 15–30 seconds, then repeat with the other leg, speaking up as soon as the stretch feels strong.
Keep your lower back and other leg on the floor; if the knee complains, cross the shin less or hug the leg in yourself without a partner.

references.title: Passive Stretching: Benefits, Examples, and More
How to Stretch Glutes: 7 Ways to Ease Tightness and Tension

fedb:Lying_Glute.note: Partner-assisted PNF version of a lying figure-four/piriformis stretch.

steps: Lie on your back with legs straight, raise one straight leg, and let your kneeling partner hold the ankle or rest your leg on their shoulder.
Press the raised leg down into your partner, as if bending the knee, for about 6–10 seconds while they keep it still.
Relax and breathe out as your partner slowly moves the leg toward your head; feel the stretch along the back of the thigh and into the calf.
Hold 15–30 seconds, repeat 2–3 rounds, then switch legs.
Keep your hips and the other leg flat on the floor, allow a soft bend in the raised knee if needed, and tell your partner when it feels strong.

references.title: Passive Stretching: Benefits, Examples, and More
PNF Stretching: Technique and Guidelines

steps: Lie face down with your forehead on your hands and your partner kneeling beside you, then bend one knee so your heel moves toward your buttock.
Your partner holds your knee and ankle while you gently try to straighten the knee for about 6–10 seconds without the leg moving.
Relax and breathe out as your partner eases your heel closer to your buttock; feel the stretch along the front of the thigh and hip.
Hold 15–30 seconds, repeat 2–3 rounds, then switch legs.
Keep your hips pressed into the floor and don't arch your lower back; ask your partner to stop before any knee pain.

references.title: Passive Stretching: Benefits, Examples, and More

steps: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft and hands on your hips.
Keeping your hips facing forward, slowly turn your ribs and shoulders to one side until you feel a gentle stretch.
You should feel it through the middle of your back and along the sides of your waist.
Breathe slowly, hold 10–15 seconds, return to centre and repeat to the other side.
Turn smoothly from the upper back instead of jerking or twisting at the knees; sit on a chair if you find your hips keep turning.

references.title: Best Exercises for Parkinson's Disease

fedb:Middle_Back_Stretch.note: Reference shows a standing trunk twist with arms out (close variant). Each side is held separately, so perSide is set to true.

steps: Sit or stand tall and hold a stick roller or rolling pin in both hands behind your neck, just below the base of your skull.
Angle the roller slightly to one side so it presses on the muscle beside your spine, never on the bony spine itself.
Roll slowly down toward the top of your shoulders, pausing on tight spots for 10–30 seconds while breathing slowly.
Work one side and then the other with light to moderate pressure for the set time.
Never press on the front or sides of your throat; for a gentler option, lie on your back with a foam roller under your neck and slowly turn your head.

references.title: Foam Roller Benefits, Risks, and How To

fedb:Neck-SMR.note: Reference describes the lying foam-roller version of neck self-massage; the entry uses a handheld roller.

steps: Lie on your back on a sturdy flat bench or step, close to one edge, and let the leg and arm on that side hang over the side.
Bend the hanging knee and hold the top of that foot with the same-side hand, keeping the other foot flat on the bench.
Draw your belly in to keep your lower back flat, then press the foot into your hand to feel a stretch along the front of the thigh.
To reach the hip flexor too, lift that hip slightly toward the ceiling; breathe, hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.
Don't let your lower back arch off the bench; loop a towel around the foot if you can't reach it.
fedb:On-Your-Back_Quad_Stretch.note: No reference found/verified (shared web-search budget ran out). One leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Lie on your right side with your head on your arm and your right knee bent forward to 90 degrees on the floor to steady you.
Bend your left knee and hold the top of your left foot or ankle with your left hand, keeping your knees roughly level.
Gently press your left hip forward and push the foot back into your hand until you feel a stretch along the front of the thigh and hip.
Breathe slowly, hold 20–30 seconds, then roll over and switch sides.
Don't arch your lower back to get more stretch; if you can't reach your foot, loop a towel or strap around it.

references.title: Side-lying Quadriceps Stretch

steps: Stand side-on to a wall or doorframe, about a foot away, and place one forearm on the wall above your head with the elbow bent.
Keeping your feet planted, slowly lean your chest and hips toward the wall so the arm slides further overhead.
You should feel the stretch along the side of your back under the armpit and down toward your waist.
Breathe slowly, hold 20–30 seconds, then switch arms.
Keep the shoulder relaxed away from your ear and don't arch your lower back; stand closer to the wall if it feels too intense.
fedb:One_Arm_Against_Wall.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out). Name is vague; written as a standing wall lat stretch matching the original steps.

steps: Lie face down and tuck your left hand under your left hip bone to cushion the hip and pubic bone.
Bend your right knee and reach back with your right hand to hold the top of your right foot or ankle.
Press the foot back into your hand to lift the thigh, and at the same time lift your chest and shoulders off the floor.
Feel the stretch across the front of the right thigh and hip, chest and shoulder; breathe steadily, hold 15–30 seconds, then switch sides.
Keep your neck long and lift only as high as your lower back allows; loop a strap around the foot if you can't reach it.
fedb:One_Half_Locust.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out). The movement is essentially Half Bow (Ardha Dhanurasana); holding both feet is full Bow. One side at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Stand under a pull-up bar, on a step if needed, and grip the bar with one hand using an overhand grip.
Keep your feet on the floor or step and bend your knees so most of your body weight hangs from that arm.
Relax the arm and lean gently away to feel the stretch along the side of your back, under the arm and into the upper arm.
Breathe slowly, hold 10–20 seconds, then switch hands.
Always keep some weight on your feet so the shoulder isn't jerked, and take more weight back onto your legs if the shoulder hurts.
fedb:One_Handed_Hang.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out). Feet-supported one-arm hang used as a lat stretch.

steps: Lie on your back on a mat with both legs straight.
Bend one knee toward your chest and hold it with your hands behind the thigh, just under the knee, while the other leg stays long on the floor.
Gently pull the knee closer until you feel a stretch in the buttock and lower back, and at the front of the hip of the straight leg.
Breathe slowly, hold 20–30 seconds, then switch legs.
Keep your head and the straight leg down; if your back is uncomfortable, bend the other knee and keep that foot flat.

references.title: Supine Hip Flexor Stretch
6 Ways to Stretch the Gluteus Medius and When to See a Doctor

steps: Sit tall on the floor with your partner behind you, raise one arm overhead and bend the elbow so your hand drops behind your head toward your back.
Your partner holds your upper arm near the elbow and your wrist while you try to pull the arm down to your side for about 6–10 seconds.
Relax and breathe out as your partner gently presses the upper arm back and up; feel it along the side of your back and back of the arm.
Hold 15–30 seconds, repeat 2–3 rounds, then switch arms.
Keep your ribs down and back upright instead of leaning away, and tell your partner to stop at mild tension.
fedb:Overhead_Lat.note: Partner-assisted PNF stretch; no reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out). One arm at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, interlace your fingers in front of you and turn your palms outward.
Press your palms up toward the ceiling and straighten your arms while keeping your shoulders down away from your ears.
Tuck your tailbone slightly and draw your belly in so your ribs don't flare, feeling the stretch along your arms, sides and torso.
Breathe deeply, reaching a little taller on each exhale, and hold for 15–30 seconds.
Don't lean back or arch your lower back; if your shoulders are tight, let your hands stay slightly in front of your head.
fedb:Overhead_Stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out); standard standing reach.

steps: Sit tall on the floor with your partner behind you, raise one arm overhead and bend the elbow so your hand reaches down your back.
Your partner holds your elbow and wrist while you try to straighten the arm toward the ceiling for about 6–10 seconds without it moving.
Relax and breathe out as your partner gently eases your hand further down your back; feel it along the back of the upper arm.
Hold 15–30 seconds, repeat 2–3 rounds, then switch arms.
Keep your head upright and ribs down; without a partner, gently press the elbow with your other hand instead.
fedb:Overhead_Triceps.note: Partner-assisted PNF stretch; no reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out). One arm at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, and heels roughly under your knees.
Draw your belly in and tilt your pelvis so your lower back presses into the floor and only your tailbone starts to lift.
Keep peeling your spine off the mat one section at a time into a bridge, leaving your head, neck and shoulders on the floor.
Breathe steadily and hold for the set time, feeling your lower back lengthen and glutes work, then roll down slowly, tailbone last.
Don't push your hips so high that your lower back arches; stop at a straight line from shoulders to knees.

references.title: Supine Pelvic Tilts
How To Do a Glute Bridge

fedb:Pelvic_Tilt_Into_Bridge.note: References cover the two parts (pelvic tilt, then bridge) separately.

steps: Lie on your side propped on your forearm with a foam roller under the outside of your bottom lower leg, just below the knee.
Cross your top leg in front with its foot on the floor, or stack it on the bottom leg for more pressure, and lift your hips slightly.
Roll slowly from below the knee to just above the ankle along the outside of your shin, feeling pressure in the muscles there.
Breathe steadily and pause on tender spots for 20 to 30 seconds for the set time, then switch legs.
Keep the roller off the bony bump on the outside of the knee and the ankle bone, and ease off if you feel tingling.

references.title: A Breakdown of Pronation Distortion Syndrome

fedb:Peroneals-SMR.note: Source includes peroneal foam rolling within a corrective program rather than as a standalone how-to. One leg at a time, so perSide true.

steps: Sit on the floor with one leg straight out in front and loop a strap, towel or band around the ball of that foot.
With the heel just off the floor, pull the strap toward the inside of your leg so the sole turns inward and the inner edge of the foot draws toward you.
You should feel the stretch along the outside of your lower leg and ankle.
Breathe slowly, hold 15–30 seconds, then switch legs.
Move gently and stop short of any ankle pain; bend the knee slightly if tight hamstrings make sitting upright hard.
fedb:Peroneals_Stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out). One leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Sit on a foam roller with your hands on the floor behind you and knees bent, then cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Lean toward the side of the crossed leg so your weight rests on that buttock.
Roll slowly in small movements over the buttock until you find a tender spot deep in the glute; gently pull the crossed knee toward your chest to increase the stretch.
Breathe slowly and hold tender spots for 20 to 30 seconds for the set time, then switch sides.
Ease off if you feel tingling down the leg, and uncross the leg for lighter pressure.

references.title: Piriformis Massage: Self-Massage and Stretches for Piriformis Syndrome

fedb:Piriformis-SMR.note: One side at a time, so perSide true.

steps: Sit on the floor with one leg straight out in front and loop a strap, towel or band around the ball of that foot.
With the heel just off the floor, pull the strap toward the outside of your leg so the sole turns outward and the outer edge of the foot draws toward you.
Keep the toes drawn back too, and feel the stretch along the inside of your calf and ankle.
Breathe slowly, hold 15–30 seconds, then switch legs.
Move gently and stop short of any ankle pain; bend the knee slightly if tight hamstrings make sitting upright hard.
fedb:Posterior_Tibialis_Stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out). One leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Kneel behind an exercise ball and roll your torso forward over it until your hips rest on top and become the highest point of your body.
Place your hands on the floor in front and your toes on the floor behind, with arms and legs straight or slightly bent to suit the ball size.
Let your head and spine relax over the ball so you feel a gentle stretch in your lower back while your shoulders and core keep you steady.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time, about 20–30 seconds, then walk your hands back and kneel to come out.
Bend your knees or use a smaller ball if balancing is hard, and keep your weight centred so you don't roll off.
fedb:Pyramid.note: Unusual name for a draped 'inverted V' over a stability ball; no reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out).

steps: Lie on your side with your head on your bottom arm and loop a belt, strap or band around your top foot.
Bend the top knee to bring that heel toward your buttock, holding the strap with the ends over your shoulder or above your head.
Gently pull the strap and press your top hip forward to feel the stretch along the front of the thigh.
Breathe slowly, hold 15–30 seconds, then roll over and switch legs.
Keep your knees level and don't arch your lower back; bend the bottom knee forward for extra stability.

references.title: Side-lying Quadriceps Stretch

fedb:Quad_Stretch.note: Reference shows the same side-lying stretch holding the foot by hand rather than with a strap. One leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Lie face down propped on your forearms with a foam roller under the front of one thigh, other leg bent out to the side for support.
Relax the thigh and use your arms to move your body so the roller travels slowly from just above the knee to just below the hip.
Feel pressure through the front of the thigh, and rotate the leg slightly in and out to reach the inner and outer parts.
Breathe steadily and pause on tender spots for 20 to 30 seconds for the set time, then switch legs.
Brace your core so your lower back does not sag, and keep the roller off the kneecap; roll both legs together for less pressure.

references.title: Foam Roller Techniques and Tips for the Lower Body

fedb:Quadriceps-SMR.note: Rolled one leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Start on your hands and knees on a mat, hands under shoulders and knees under hips, with your neck in line with your back.
Brace your belly and lift one leg up and back, straightening the knee and hip until the leg is roughly in line with your body.
Feel your buttock and thigh working and a gentle opening at the front of the hip, then lower the knee with control.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower, repeating slowly for the set time (about 5–10 raises), then switch legs.
Don't lift so high that your lower back arches or your hips twist; keep both hips level.

references.title: Quadruped Bent-knee Hip Extensions

fedb:Rear_Leg_Raises.note: Performed as repetitions although mode is time. Reference is the bent-knee variant; this entry straightens the leg. One leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Lie on your back with a foam roller across your upper back, knees bent and feet flat, and cross your arms over your chest to spread your shoulder blades apart.
Lift your hips slightly and use your feet to roll slowly between the bottom of your shoulder blades and the top of your upper back.
Lean a little to one side to target the muscles between your spine and shoulder blade, then the other side, feeling pressure in the mid and upper back.
Breathe slowly and pause on tender spots for 20 to 30 seconds within the set time.
Do not roll down onto your lower back; if your neck strains, support your head with your hands instead.

references.title: A Breakdown of Bicep Tendonitis

fedb:Rhomboids-SMR.note: Source shows a supine thoracic (mid/upper back) foam roll within a corrective program, the same setup as this entry.

steps: Stand tall with your feet together, holding a broomstick or body bar behind your hips with an overhand grip wider than your shoulders.
Keeping your arms straight and chest lifted, slowly raise the stick up and away from your back as far as is comfortable.
You should feel the stretch across the front of your shoulders, chest and biceps.
Breathe steadily and hold at your highest comfortable point for the set time, then lower slowly.
Don't bend forward or force the arms higher when it gets hard; a wider grip makes it easier.
fedb:Round_The_World_Shoulder_Stretch.note: Name suggests a full over-the-head pass-through, but the original steps/images describe raising a stick behind the back; the old 'behind your head' wording was corrected. No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out).

steps: From standing, step one foot back into a long lunge and lower your hands to the floor on either side of your front foot.
Keep your front heel down (slide the back leg further away if it lifts) and lower the back knee to the floor if that is more comfortable.
Push your hips up and back to straighten the front leg and stretch the back of that thigh, then lower them to stretch the front of the back hip.
Breathe slowly, moving gently between the two positions for the set time, then switch legs.
Keep your back long rather than rounding it, and put your hands on blocks or a step if they don't reach the floor.
fedb:Runners_Stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out). One leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Lie on your back with your arms by your sides, palms down or tucked under your hips, and press your lower back into the floor.
With a slight bend in the knees, lift both heels about 15 cm (6 in) off the floor.
Raise one leg to about 45 degrees while lowering the other to just above the floor, then switch in a smooth scissoring motion.
Breathe steadily and keep alternating for the set time, feeling the work in your lower abs.
Stop if your lower back lifts off the floor; keep your legs higher or the movement smaller to make it easier.
fedb:Scissor_Kick.note: This is a core exercise rather than a stretch. Some sources call a side-to-side leg-crossing move 'scissor kick'; this entry is the up-and-down version. No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out).

steps: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat, and reach both arms straight back behind you, palms facing each other, while your partner holds your wrists.
Try to bend your elbows against your partner's grip for about 6–10 seconds while they keep your arms still.
Relax and breathe out as your partner slowly lifts your wrists up and back; feel the stretch in the front of your arms, shoulders and chest.
Hold 15–30 seconds and repeat 2–3 rounds, keeping your chest tall.
Tell your partner to stop at mild tension, especially if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulders.
fedb:Seated_Biceps.note: Partner-assisted PNF stretch; no reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out).

steps: Sit tall on a mat, bend one knee with that foot flat on the floor and stretch the other leg straight out.
Flex the ankle of the straight leg so your toes point up, and loop a towel or band around the ball of the foot, or hold your toes.
Gently pull the toes toward you until you feel a stretch in the calf and possibly behind the knee.
Breathe slowly, hold 15–30 seconds, then switch legs.
Sit up tall rather than rounding your back to pull, and keep the knee straight but not locked.
fedb:Seated_Calf_Stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out). One leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Sit on a mat with your right leg straight out in front and your left knee bent so the sole of that foot rests against your right inner thigh.
Sit up tall, then hinge forward from your hips and reach toward your right ankle or shin.
Stop when you feel a stretch along the back of the right thigh, and possibly into the calf.
Breathe slowly, hold 15–30 seconds, then switch legs.
Lead with your chest rather than rounding your back to reach your toes; loop a strap around the foot if you're tight.
fedb:Seated_Floor_Hamstring_Stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out). One leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Sit tall on the floor with knees bent and your partner standing behind you, arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, palms down.
Move your arms back as far as is comfortable and let your partner hold your wrists there.
Try to bring your arms forward against your partner for about 6–10 seconds while they keep them still.
Relax and breathe out as your partner gently draws your arms further back; feel the stretch across the front of your shoulders and chest for 15–30 seconds.
Keep your elbows straight and chest tall, and tell your partner to stop at mild tension.
fedb:Seated_Front_Deltoid.note: Partner-assisted PNF stretch; no reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out).

steps: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat, cross one ankle over the opposite knee, and have your partner stand behind you.
Lean forward from your hips with a long back while your partner places their hands on your shoulders.
Push your torso back against their hands for about 6–10 seconds while they hold you still.
Relax and breathe out as your partner gently eases you further forward; feel the stretch deep in the buttock of the crossed leg for 15–30 seconds.
Keep the crossed foot flexed, tell your partner to stop at mild tension, then repeat with the other leg crossed.

references.title: How to Stretch Glutes: 7 Ways to Ease Tightness and Tension

fedb:Seated_Glute.note: Partner-assisted PNF version; the reference shows the solo seated figure-four. One leg crossed at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Sit on the floor with both legs straight in front of you, toes pointing up, and your partner standing behind you.
Hinge forward from your hips as far as is comfortable while your partner places their hands on your upper back or shoulders.
Push your torso back into their hands for about 6–10 seconds while they hold you still.
Relax and breathe out as your partner slowly eases you further forward; feel the stretch along the backs of your thighs and calves for 15–30 seconds.
Reach forward with a long spine rather than rounding, and tell your partner the moment it feels strong.
fedb:Seated_Hamstring.note: Partner-assisted PNF stretch; no reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out).

steps: Sit on the floor with both legs straight and loop a belt, strap or band around the ball of one foot, holding an end in each hand.
Sit tall and lean forward slightly from your hips.
Pull the strap to draw your toes back toward you until you feel a stretch along the back of the thigh and into the calf.
Breathe slowly, hold 15–30 seconds, then switch legs.
Keep the knee straight but not locked and don't round your back; bend the other knee if sitting upright is hard.
fedb:Seated_Hamstring_and_Calf_Stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out). One leg at a time, so perSide should be true.

steps: Sit tall on a mat with the soles of your feet together, heels about a hand's length or two in front of your hips.
Place your left hand on the floor beside your hip and rest your right hand lightly behind your head, elbow pointing out.
Lift your right elbow toward the ceiling and bend your upper body to the left until you feel a stretch along the right side of your waist and ribs.
Breathe slowly and hold for 15–30 seconds, then come back to center and repeat to the other side.
Keep your chest facing forward rather than rolling it toward the floor; sit on a folded towel or cross your legs if your back rounds.

references.title: 5 Workday Stretches That Relax Your Mind and Body

fedb:Seated_Overhead_Stretch.note: Despite the name this is a seated side bend (lateral flexion), mainly obliques/lats. It is done one side then the other, so perSide should be true. The ACE reference shows the same side bend seated on a chair with both hands behind the head.

steps: Stand or sit tall with your arms hanging relaxed by your sides, or hands resting in your lap, and your chin level.
Slowly lift your shoulders toward your ears, draw them back, drop them down and bring them forward, tracing one smooth, full circle.
You should feel your shoulders, upper back and the base of your neck loosen as you move.
Breathe steadily and keep circling for the set time, switching direction halfway; roll both shoulders together or one at a time.
Keep the rest of your body still and the circles slow and round; don't jerk the shoulders or lift your arms.

references.title: General shoulder exercises - Resource Library - Sheffield Children's NHS Foundation Trust

steps: Stand or sit tall with your arms hanging loosely at your sides and your neck long.
Lift both shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as is comfortable, keeping your arms and elbows relaxed.
Pause for a second or two to feel the tops of your shoulders and upper traps tighten, then let the shoulders drop and fully relax.
Breathe in as you lift and out as you lower, repeating slowly and steadily for the set time.
Move straight up and down without rolling the shoulders or pushing your head forward.

references.title: Exercise Library:Standing Shrug
Seated Workouts for Beginners: 5 Tips for Starting Exercise from Scratch

fedb:Shoulder_Raise.note: This is an unweighted shoulder shrug; it mainly works the upper trapezius, not the lats (secondary muscle looks off). The ACE Standing Shrug page is the dumbbell version of the same movement; the second ACE page has a seated raise-and-lower version.

steps: Stand or sit tall with your shoulders relaxed and level.
Bring your left arm straight across your chest at about shoulder height and hook your right hand or forearm just above the left elbow.
Gently draw the arm closer to your chest until you feel a stretch at the back of your left shoulder and upper arm.
Breathe normally and hold for 15–30 seconds, then switch arms.
Keep the stretched shoulder down and your chest facing forward; don't press on the elbow joint itself or twist your body to fake range.
fedb:Shoulder_Stretch.note: Standard cross-body shoulder stretch; current steps were incomplete (no pulling hand, no hold, no switch). Done one arm at a time, so perSide should be true. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Lie on your left side with your left knee bent in front of you for stability and your abs lightly braced.
Straighten your right leg and rest the right foot on the floor just behind your left leg.
Reach both arms overhead, hold your right wrist with your left hand and gently pull to lengthen your whole right side.
Feel the stretch from your right hip through your waist and under your armpit; breathe into that side and hold for 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.
Stay stacked on your side rather than rolling forward or back; if your shoulder complains, just reach the arm overhead without pulling.
fedb:Side-Lying_Floor_Stretch.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand facing a wall or chair back, holding it with both hands, and put your weight on one leg.
Keeping the free leg straight and toes pointing forward, swing it out to the side as high as is comfortable.
Let it swing back down and across in front of your standing leg, then out again in one smooth pendulum motion.
Start small and widen the swing gradually, feeling your inner and outer hip loosen; breathe easily, keep going for the set time, then switch legs.
Keep your torso upright and hips facing forward instead of leaning sideways to get the leg higher.
fedb:Side_Leg_Raises.note: Despite the name, this entry describes a dynamic lateral (side-to-side) leg swing, not a side-lying leg raise; consider renaming to 'Lateral Leg Swings'. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Lie on your right side with your head resting on your right arm and your right knee bent in front of you for balance.
Bend your left knee and lift the leg, holding the back of the thigh or knee (easier) or the inside of the foot (harder).
Draw your left knee up toward your left shoulder, letting the leg open, until you feel a stretch along your inner thigh and back of the leg.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds; to go deeper, straighten the left leg toward the ceiling, then roll over and switch sides.
Keep your hips stacked rather than rolling onto your back, and loop a strap around the foot if you can't reach it.
fedb:Side_Lying_Groin_Stretch.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and down, looking straight ahead.
Slowly tilt your head to bring your right ear toward your right shoulder without lifting the shoulder to meet it.
For more, reach your right hand over your head and let its weight add a light pull; feel the stretch along the left side of your neck.
Breathe slowly and hold for 15–30 seconds, then return to center and repeat to the left.
Never yank on your head or let your chin turn; keep it a pure sideways tilt and ease off if you feel tingling.

references.title: Exercise Library:Lateral Neck Flexion

steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Cross your left arm in front of your body and grip your left wrist with your right hand at about hip level, left elbow slightly bent.
Slowly straighten the left arm and use your right hand to pull it across and up toward shoulder height, letting the left shoulder blade slide forward.
Feel the stretch across the back of the left shoulder and upper back; breathe slowly and hold for 15–30 seconds, then switch sides.
Pull gently and keep the shoulder down away from your ear; ease off if you feel pinching in the shoulder joint.
fedb:Side_Wrist_Pull.note: Obscure stretch with no common equivalent name (closest is a diagonal cross-body shoulder/upper-back stretch). No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out, and arms forward or hands on hips for balance.
Push your hips back and bend your knees as if starting to sit in a chair, keeping your chest up and heels down.
Stop a little above parallel, then press through your feet to stand back up briskly; you should feel your thighs and glutes working.
Breathe in on the way down and out on the way up, keeping a steady rhythm (roughly 5–10 reps) for the set time.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes instead of caving in, and go less deep if your heels lift.
fedb:Sit_Squats.note: Dynamic warm-up done for reps (partial bodyweight squats), not a held stretch, although the entry's mode is time. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Sit near the front of a chair with your back straight and both feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Lace your fingers behind your head with your elbows wide and your chin slightly tucked.
Turn your upper body to the right as far as is comfortable a few times, then fold forward and reach your left elbow toward the floor inside your right knee.
Feel the stretch through your mid and upper back and the sides of your trunk; breathe out as you twist and hold each end position briefly.
Sit back up and repeat to the left, keeping your hips square on the seat and never forcing the twist.
fedb:Spinal_Stretch.note: Done one direction then the other, so perSide should be true. The original 'reach your elbow inside your knee' did not say which elbow/knee; clarified as opposite elbow to the knee you turn toward. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, then hop into a split stance with one foot forward and one back, both knees slightly bent.
Lower your hips a few inches, then spring up and switch legs in the air, landing softly with the other foot in front.
Keep the movement continuous and absorb each landing by bending your knees; you'll feel your thighs, glutes and calves working.
Breathe in a steady rhythm and keep alternating for the set time, about 5–10 times per leg.
Keep your front knee over your ankle and torso upright; for an easier version, skip the jump and step between alternating split squats.
fedb:Split_Squats.note: As described this is a jumping split squat (split jump) warm-up drill, not a static split squat; the name and primary muscle (hamstrings; quads/glutes do most work) don't fit well. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and clasp your hands behind your back.
Straighten your arms, then rotate them so your palms turn to face down.
Slowly lift your arms up behind you, keeping the elbows straight, until you feel a stretch along the front of your upper arms, shoulders and chest.
Breathe evenly and hold for 15–30 seconds, then lower your arms slowly.
Stay upright instead of bending forward and keep your shoulders down; hold a towel between your hands if they won't meet.
fedb:Standing_Biceps_Stretch.note: Equipment is listed as 'other' but this needs nothing (body only, optional towel). No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand tall with your back to a bench or step, about two to three feet in front of it.
Reach one leg back and rest the top of that foot, or the ball of the foot, on the bench, whichever is more comfortable.
Bend your standing knee slightly and tuck your tailbone under until you feel a stretch along the front of the raised leg's thigh and hip.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds, then switch legs.
Keep the standing knee behind your toes and your torso upright; use a lower step or hold a wall if balance is hard.
fedb:Standing_Elevated_Quad_Stretch.note: One leg at a time (steps say switch sides), so perSide should be true. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand in front of a low step and place your right heel on it with the knee straight and toes pointing up.
Keep your left knee slightly bent, rest your left hand on your left thigh, and hinge forward from the hips with a straight back.
Reach your right hand to your right toes and gently pull them toward your shin until you feel a stretch in the calf and back of the thigh.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds, then switch legs.
Don't round your back to reach; loop a towel around the foot if you can't reach your toes.
fedb:Standing_Gastrocnemius_Calf_Stretch.note: One leg at a time, so perSide should be true (original steps never said to switch). No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Loop a belt, band or towel around the ball of one foot and stand with that foot a short step in front of the other.
