Bend your back knee, keep the front leg straight, and lift the front toes so only the heel stays on the floor.
Hinge forward from your hips with a straight back and gently pull the strap to draw the toes toward you.
Feel the stretch along the back of the front thigh and calf; breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds, then switch feet.
Keep your back flat rather than rounding down toward the knee, and lean less if the stretch feels sharp.
fedb:Standing_Hamstring_and_Calf_Stretch.note: One leg at a time (steps say repeat with the other foot), so perSide should be true. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand tall beside a wall or chair and hold it with one hand, weight on the leg nearest the support.
Lift your other knee to hip height so the thigh is roughly level with the floor.
Slowly swing the knee out to the side, then down and back in toward the front, tracing the biggest circle you comfortably can.
Feel your hip, inner and outer thigh loosen; breathe steadily and circle for the set time, reversing direction halfway, then switch legs.
Keep your standing knee soft and your torso upright; don't lean away from the support to make the circle bigger.
fedb:Standing_Hip_Circles.note: One leg at a time (steps say repeat on the other side), so perSide should be true. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand tall with your left foot a short stride in front of your right, feet hip-width apart.
Bend both knees and let your right heel lift off the floor.
Tuck your tailbone under and press your right hip forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the right hip and upper thigh.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds, then switch legs.
Keep your torso upright and avoid arching your lower back; for a deeper stretch, try a half-kneeling version instead.
fedb:Standing_Hip_Flexors.note: One leg at a time, so perSide should be true. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than hip-width apart and your knees softly bent.
Rest your right hand on your right hip, then raise your left arm and place the left hand lightly behind your head.
Bend your upper body to the right, lifting your left elbow toward the ceiling, until you feel a stretch along your left side.
Breathe into the stretched side and hold for 15–30 seconds, then switch sides.
Keep your weight even on both feet and your chest facing forward; don't push your hips out sideways or tip forward.
fedb:Standing_Lateral_Stretch.note: Done one side then the other, so perSide should be true. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your hips.
Soften your knees so they are slightly bent and relaxed.
Rock your pelvis gently forward and back a few times, then tuck your tailbone under and hold it there with your glutes and abs lightly engaged.
Feel your lower back lengthen and flatten slightly; breathe normally and hold for 10–20 seconds, then relax.
Move only your pelvis, keeping your shoulders and ribs still, and don't lock your knees.
fedb:Standing_Pelvic_Tilt.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and one foot a short step in front of the other, hands on a wall if you like.
Bend both knees and sink your hips straight down, keeping your back heel pressed into the floor.
Feel the stretch low in the back leg's calf, just above the heel along the Achilles tendon.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds, then switch legs.
Keep the back foot pointing forward and the heel down; if you feel it high in the calf, bend the back knee more.
fedb:Standing_Soleus_And_Achilles_Stretc.note: One leg at a time (steps say switch sides), so perSide should be true. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and some clear space in front of and behind you.
Keeping your legs straight but knees not locked, hinge at the hips and let your upper body fold down toward your toes.
Let your arms, head and neck hang loosely and feel the stretch along the backs of your legs and lower back.
Breathe slowly and hold for 15–30 seconds, then bend your knees slightly and roll up gradually.
Don't bounce to reach farther; bend your knees or rest your hands on your shins if your hamstrings are tight.
fedb:Standing_Toe_Touches.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands on your hips.
Breathe in deeply, then breathe out completely while drawing your belly button in toward your spine as far as you can.
Keep your belly pulled in, feeling the deep abdominal muscles tighten, while you take small, shallow breaths.
Hold for about 20 seconds, then relax and breathe normally; build up toward 40–60 seconds over time.
Don't hold your breath or hunch your shoulders; it's easier to learn on all fours or lying on your back.
fedb:Stomach_Vacuum.note: Isometric deep-core (transverse abdominis) exercise rather than a stretch. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Lie face down on a mat with your arms stretched forward, legs straight, and your forehead just above the floor.
Breathe out and lift your arms, chest and legs a few inches off the floor at the same time, squeezing your glutes.
Hold for 2–5 seconds while breathing, feeling the muscles along your spine, glutes and hamstrings working.
Lower slowly as you breathe in and repeat steadily for the set time.
Keep your neck long by looking at the floor, not forward; for an easier version, lift only your arms or only your legs.
fedb:Superman.note: Back-strengthening exercise rather than a stretch. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Sit tall on the floor and open your legs wide in a V, kneecaps and toes pointing up.
Place your hands on the floor in front of you and hinge forward from your hips, walking your hands out.
Lean forward only until you feel a stretch along the backs and inner sides of your thighs.
Breathe slowly, easing a little deeper with each exhale, and hold for 15–30 seconds.
Keep your back long rather than rounding; sit on a folded towel or bend your knees slightly if you can't sit upright.

references.title: Seated Straddle Stretch

steps: Lie on your back with your arms by your sides, then raise your legs together until they point almost straight up, knees slightly bent.
Reach your arms straight up toward your feet; this is your starting position.
Breathe out and curl your head and shoulders off the floor, reaching your hands toward your toes while your lower back stays pressed down.
Lower slowly as you breathe in and repeat smoothly for the set time, feeling your upper abs work.
Lead with your chest rather than your chin and don't swing your legs; bend your knees more if your hamstrings are tight.
fedb:Toe_Touchers.note: Abdominal crunch variation done for reps, not a stretch, although mode is time. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and knees soft, holding an exercise ball with straight arms in front of your chest.
Slowly rotate your torso to one side, keeping your eyes on the ball, then turn back through the middle to the other side.
Keep your hips facing forward so you feel the twist in your waist and mid-back.
Breathe out as you turn and in as you come back, moving smoothly for the set time.
Don't swing for momentum; shorten the range or hold the ball closer to your chest if your lower back feels strained.
fedb:Torso_Rotation.note: Dynamic rotation done for reps (original says 10–20), although mode is time. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand or sit tall, bring your right arm across your chest and bend the elbow so your right hand reaches over your left shoulder.
Hold your right elbow with your left hand and gently pull it farther across your body toward your chest.
Feel the stretch along the back of your right upper arm and the back of the shoulder.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds, then switch arms.
Keep both shoulders down and your torso facing forward instead of twisting toward the arm being pulled.

references.title: 4 Triceps Stretches for Tight Muscles

fedb:Tricep_Side_Stretch.note: This is the cross-body (horizontal) triceps stretch with the elbow bent. Healthline shows it with a straighter arm.

steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, raise one arm overhead and bend the elbow so your hand drops behind your head toward your upper back.
Place your other hand on the bent elbow and gently press it back and down to slide the hand farther down your back.
Feel the stretch along the back of the upper arm and down the side of your torso toward the armpit.
Breathe evenly and hold for 15–30 seconds, then switch arms.
Keep your head upright and ribs down instead of pushing your head forward or arching your lower back.

references.title: Exercise Library: Overhead Triceps Stretch
4 Triceps Stretches for Tight Muscles

fedb:Triceps_Stretch.note: Current steps say to switch sides, so this should be per side.

steps: Sit on the floor with your legs straight out in front of you and your knees and feet together.
Fold forward from your hips and wrap both arms under your thighs so you are hugging the backs of your legs.
Use the hug to draw your chest down toward your knees until you feel a stretch along your hamstrings and lower back.
For more upper-back stretch, keep hugging and gently pull your back away from your legs, rounding between your shoulder blades.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds; bend your knees as much as you need so your arms can reach without straining your back.
fedb:Upper_Back-Leg_Grab.note: This name only appears in free-exercise-db. The closest standard movement is a seated forward fold with the arms hugging the thighs. Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Stand or sit tall, interlace your fingers in front of your chest and turn your palms away from you so your thumbs point down.
Straighten your arms and push your hands forward at shoulder height while you round your upper back and let your head drop between your arms.
Feel the stretch spread across your upper back and between your shoulder blades.
Breathe into your back and hold for 15–30 seconds, reaching a little farther each time you exhale.
Reach by spreading your shoulder blades apart, not by shrugging toward your ears; if turning the palms out strains your wrists, keep them facing you.

references.title: The Ultimate 'Deskercise' Routine: Stretches for the Office
Mindful Movements: To Help You Heal and Recover

fedb:Upper_Back_Stretch.note: The secondary muscle list repeats the primary one (middle back).

steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and raise both arms straight overhead with your palms pressed together.
Reach your hands up toward the ceiling, then ease them slightly back behind your ears while keeping your arms straight.
Feel the stretch through your shoulders, the sides of your back and across your chest.
Breathe slowly and hold for 15–30 seconds.
Keep your ribs down and lower back neutral instead of leaning back; if pressing the palms together is too hard, interlace your fingers and turn the palms up.
fedb:Upward_Stretch.note: A generic free-exercise-db entry that is close to a standing overhead reach or Upward Salute. Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms out to the sides in a T, palms down.
Keep one leg as straight as you can, lift it and sweep it across your body toward the opposite hand, letting your hips rotate.
Feel the stretch through the outer hip, glutes, hamstrings and lower back while both shoulders stay on the floor.
Bring the leg back to centre and repeat with the other leg, alternating at a steady, controlled pace and breathing normally for the set time.
Don't fling the leg; bend the knee slightly or reach only as far as you can keep the opposite shoulder down.
fedb:Windmills.note: This is a dynamic, alternating drill, also called a supine leg crossover, so time mode here means the length of the set rather than a hold. The old steps said to move 'quickly'; these steps say to move with control. Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Step one foot far forward into a long lunge with the back knee lifted, and place both hands on the floor inside the front foot.
Lower the elbow on the front-leg side toward the inside of that foot, then rotate your chest and reach that arm up to the ceiling.
Return the hand to the floor, shift your hips back and straighten the front leg with toes lifted to stretch the hamstring.
Feel the back-leg hip flexor, the front-leg groin and hamstring, and your upper back; breathe slowly and hold each part for 10–20 seconds.
Keep the front knee over the ankle, put the back knee down if balance is hard, then repeat the whole sequence on the other side.

references.title: The 10-Point, 10-Minute Pre-Run Warm-Up to Beat Common Running Injuries

fedb:Worlds_Greatest_Stretch.note: The old steps left out the usual thoracic rotation (arm reaching to the ceiling), so it has been added. The old steps also do the exercise on both sides, so it should be per side. Some coaches use it as a flowing warm-up drill rather than a set of holds.

steps: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and raise your arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, palms down, forming a T.
Keep your arms still and circle both hands from the wrists in slow, wide circles in a forward direction.
Feel your wrists and forearms loosen and warm up; the movement should never feel painful.
Breathe normally and circle for 15–30 seconds, then reverse direction for the same time.
Make the circles as big as you can without moving your elbows; if your shoulders tire, do it with elbows bent at your sides.
fedb:Wrist_Circles.note: Both wrists move at the same time. Steps say to reverse direction, which the old steps left out. Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Sit with your front leg bent about 90° in front of you, outer thigh and calf on the floor, and your back leg out to the side, also bent about 90°, inner knee down and the foot pointing behind you.
Sit tall with your chest square to the front shin and your fingertips on the floor for balance; keep both sit bones heavy instead of leaning away from the front leg.
You should feel it in the outer hip and glute of the front leg, often also at the front of the back hip. For more, hinge forward from the hips over the front shin with a long back.
Breathe slowly and hold 30–60 seconds, letting the hips settle a little more on each exhale, then swap the leg positions.
Don't round your back or tip sideways to get lower; sit on a folded towel or block if you can't sit upright, and ease off if the hip pinches or the knee hurts.

references.title: The 90/90 Stretch & How It Helps Hip Mobility
90/90 Stretch: Benefits, Tips, and How-To

steps: Sit on the floor with both knees bent about 90 degrees, feet planted wider than hip-width, and hands on the floor behind you for support.
Keeping your feet in place, let both knees drop to one side so the front leg turns out and the back leg turns in, forming a 90/90 shape.
Sit tall over the front shin and feel the stretch in the outer hip of the front leg and the front of the back hip.
Lift both knees and rotate them over to the other side, exhaling as you switch and pausing briefly; each side counts as one rep.
Move slowly and never force the knees down; keep your hands behind you or sit on a cushion if you cannot sit upright.

references.title: Unlock Tight Hips for Good With the Shin Box Stretch
90/90 Stretch: Benefits, Tips, and How-To

steps: Stand tall with your core braced, weight on the balls of your feet and elbows bent about 90 degrees.
Drive one knee up until the thigh is about parallel to the floor, with the ankle flexed and toes pulled up, while rising onto the ball of the standing foot.
Swing the opposite arm forward in rhythm, then push the foot down to land under your hip and repeat with the other leg as you walk forward.
You should feel the hip flexors and calves working; breathe steadily and keep a crisp, rhythmic tempo for the set reps per leg.
Avoid leaning back or reaching the foot out in front of you; stay tall and keep the knee lift controlled.
george:a-march.note: No reputable page found that describes the A-march step by step (Stack only lists it in warm-ups, not cited); steps follow standard sprint-drill coaching. Web search limit was also reached.

steps: Stand facing a wall or the edge of a doorway and place a massage or lacrosse ball on your chest just below the collarbone, toward the front of the shoulder.
Lean into the wall until you feel firm but bearable pressure, then make small circles or slowly slide that arm up and down the wall.
You should feel a deep pressure in the chest muscle near the shoulder; pause on tender spots.
Breathe slowly and hold each tender spot for 20 to 30 seconds for the set time, then switch sides.
Stay off the collarbone, breastbone and armpit, and move the ball if you feel tingling, numbness or sharp pain.

references.title: How to Perform a Lacrosse Ball Massage on Sore Muscles

steps: Stand with your back to a wall and place a massage ball on your upper trap, the muscle between the base of your neck and the top of your shoulder blade.
Bend your knees slightly and lean back into the ball, letting that shoulder relax and drop.
Bend and straighten your knees to roll the ball slowly over tender spots, feeling the pressure across the top of your shoulder.
Breathe slowly and pause for 20 to 30 seconds on each tender spot for the set time, then switch sides.
Keep the ball off your spine and neck bones; stand more upright with your feet closer to the wall for lighter pressure.

references.title: How to Perform a Lacrosse Ball Massage on Sore Muscles

george:ball-upper-trap-release.note: Source describes wall ball work for the upper back and shoulders generally, not the upper trap by name.

steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight and together and your arms overhead, holding opposite elbows if that is comfortable.
Keep your buttocks and shoulders on the mat and walk your feet, then your upper body, toward the same side so your body curves like a banana.
Cross your outer ankle over the inner one to feel a longer stretch from the outer hip through the side ribs to the armpit on the outside of the curve.
Relax and breathe into the stretched side ribs for 1–3 minutes, then walk back to centre and repeat on the other side.
Keep both hips heavy instead of letting one buttock lift, and ease the curve back if your lower back feels pinched.
george:banana-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Stand tall holding a light band (or broomstick) in front of your thighs with a wide overhand grip and straight arms.
Brace your core and slowly raise your arms overhead and back in one smooth arc until the band reaches behind you near your lower back.
Feel the stretch across the front of your shoulders and chest, then reverse the arc to bring the band back to the front.
Breathe in as you lift and out as you pass behind; repeat smoothly for the set reps.
If you have to bend your elbows, shrug, or arch your lower back, widen your grip or use a looser band.

references.title: Shoulder Mobility Exercises and Stretches with Pictures

george:band-shoulder-pass-through.note: Source shows the stick (broomstick/PVC) version; the band version is the same movement.

steps: Loop a long resistance band over a pull-up bar or another high anchor and slip one hand through so the band sits around your wrist.
Step back and hinge at the hips with that arm straight, letting the band pull it overhead and slightly forward.
Push your hips back and let your chest sink toward the floor until you feel a stretch along the side of your back and armpit.
Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing deeply into your side ribs, then switch arms.
Keep your ribs down instead of arching your lower back; turn your chest slightly away from the arm to deepen the stretch.
george:banded-lat-stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Current steps were already correct.

steps: Sit on a folded blanket, bend your knees and swing both feet to the left so they rest beside your left hip, with the left ankle in the right foot's arch.
Inhale and lengthen your spine, keeping both sitting bones as grounded as you can.
Exhale and turn your chest to the right, placing your right hand on the floor behind you and your left hand on the outside of your right knee.
Feel the twist through your middle back and side ribs; breathe for 5–10 breaths, growing taller as you inhale and turning slightly more as you exhale.
Start the twist from your belly rather than cranking your neck, then unwind and repeat with your feet to the right, turning left.
george:bharadvajas-twist.note: Old steps were vague about direction. You turn your chest away from the side your feet are on. Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Sit with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hold the backs of your thighs and sit up tall.
Lean back slightly with a long spine and lift your feet until your shins are parallel to the floor, balancing just behind your sitting bones.
Let go of your legs and reach your arms forward at shoulder height, straightening your legs only if your chest stays lifted.
Feel your abs and hip flexors working; breathe steadily and hold for 15–30 seconds, then lower your feet with control.
Don't round your lower back or hold your breath; keep your hands behind your thighs for an easier version.
george:boat-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Sit tall on the mat or a folded blanket, bring the soles of your feet together and let your knees drop out to the sides.
Hold your feet or ankles and draw your heels toward you only as far as is comfortable.
Lengthen your spine and, for more stretch, hinge forward from your hips while keeping your back long.
Feel the stretch along your inner thighs and groin; breathe slowly and hold for 30–60 seconds.
Don't force your knees down with your hands or elbows; support them on blocks or slide your feet farther away if your hips are tight.

references.title: Seated Butterfly Stretch (ACE Exercise Library)

steps: Lie on your belly with your arms by your sides, bend your knees and reach back to hold the outsides of your ankles.
Inhale and kick your feet back into your hands, letting that pull lift your chest, head and thighs off the mat.
Feel a stretch across the fronts of your thighs, hips, chest and shoulders while your back muscles work.
Breathe steadily for 3–5 breaths (about 15–30 seconds), then exhale, lower slowly and rest with your cheek on the mat.
Keep your knees no wider than your hips and your neck long; loop a strap around your ankles if you can't reach them.
george:bow-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Lie on your side, bring your top knee up to hip height in front of you and rest it on the floor, holding it down with your bottom hand.
Bend your bottom knee behind you and reach back with your top hand to hold that foot or ankle.
Turn your chest and head toward the ceiling, letting your top shoulder sink toward the floor behind you while the top knee stays down.
Feel the stretch in the front of the bottom thigh and through your upper back and chest; breathe out to sink deeper and hold 30–60 seconds, then switch sides.
If you can't reach the foot, loop a strap around it, and rest the top knee on a cushion if it won't reach the floor.
george:bretzel-stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Current steps were already correct.

steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart with heels near your buttocks, and arms by your sides palms down.
Exhale, press through your feet and arms and lift your hips, peeling your spine off the mat from the tailbone upward.
Feel your glutes and hamstrings working and a gentle stretch across the fronts of your hips and chest.
Breathe steadily and hold for 30–60 seconds, then roll down slowly from the upper back to the tailbone.
Keep your knees pointing forward instead of falling apart and don't turn your head while lifted; rest a block under your sacrum for a supported version.
george:bridge-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Kneel with knees hip-width apart and thighs vertical, and place your hands on your lower back with fingers pointing down.
Inhale and lift your chest, drawing your elbows toward each other as you press your hips forward over your knees.
Bend back only as far as your lower back stays comfortable, reaching for your heels only if it is easy; tuck your toes to bring your heels higher.
Feel the stretch across the fronts of your hips, thighs, belly and chest, and breathe steadily for 3–5 breaths.
Don't drop your head back or crunch your lower back; come up slowly, leading with your chest, with your chin slightly tucked.
george:camel-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders, knees under hips and your spine flat.
Inhale as you let your belly sink, tilt your tailbone up and lift your chest and gaze (Cow).
Exhale as you round your spine toward the ceiling, tuck your tailbone and let your head drop (Cat).
Feel your whole spine and back muscles loosen as you flow slowly with your breath for the set reps.
Do not force your neck or chin; pad your knees or move your hands slightly forward if your knees or wrists ache.

references.title: How to Do Cat-Cow Pose and Stretch the Muscles in Your Back
Cow Pose: How to Practice Bitilasana

steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair with your feet wide and flat on the floor and your toes turned slightly out.
Place your hands or forearms on your inner thighs just above the knees.
Lean your chest forward with a long, straight back and gently press your knees outward until you feel a stretch along your inner thighs.
Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly, easing a little deeper each time you breathe out.
Keep your knees in line with your toes and don't bounce.
george:chair-adductor-stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Current steps were already correct.

steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair with your feet flat and a little wider than your hips.
Breathe out and fold forward from your hips, letting your chest rest toward your thighs and your arms and head hang toward the floor.
Relax your neck and breathe into your back; you should feel a gentle stretch along your spine and between your shoulder blades.
Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly.
Place your hands on your thighs and roll up slowly so you don't feel light-headed.
george:chair-forward-fold.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Current steps were already correct.

steps: Sit sideways on a sturdy chair without wheels so one hip hangs just off the edge of the seat.
Slide the outside leg back behind you onto the ball of the foot, with the knee pointing down toward the floor.
Sit tall and gently tuck your tailbone under until you feel a stretch at the front of the hip and thigh of the back leg.
Hold for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly, then turn around to switch sides.
Keep your torso upright instead of leaning forward, and hold the chair back for balance if needed.
george:chair-hip-flexor-stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Current steps were already correct.

steps: Stand with feet together or hip-width apart and sweep your arms overhead, palms facing each other.
Exhale, bend your knees and sit your hips back as if lowering into a chair, bringing your thighs as close to parallel with the floor as you can.
Feel your thighs and glutes working hard while your shoulders and upper back stay active.
Hold for 5–10 slow breaths (about 30 seconds), then inhale and press through your feet to stand.
Keep your weight in your heels and your ribs drawn in instead of arching your lower back; bring your hands to your hips if your shoulders tire.
george:chair-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Start in child's pose with your knees apart, hips sitting back toward your heels and both arms stretched forward on the floor.
Walk both hands over to the right side of the mat while your hips stay sitting back toward your heels.
Press your palms down and reach your fingertips away to feel a stretch along the left side of your body, from hip to armpit.
Breathe into your side ribs and hold for 20–30 seconds, then walk your hands through the middle to the left side.
Keep both hips sinking back; if they lift or shift, walk your hands less far to the side.
george:childs-pose-side-reach.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Current steps were already correct.

steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and your eyes looking straight ahead.
Keeping your chin level, glide your head straight back as if making a double chin, without nodding up or down.
You should feel the deep muscles at the front of your neck working and a gentle stretch at the base of your skull.
Hold for 3 to 5 seconds while breathing normally, then relax; repeat for the set reps.
Do not tip your head down or jam it back hard; place two fingers on your chin as a guide, or try it lying on your back if easier.

references.title: 6 Pinched Nerve in Neck Exercises
Forward Head Posture: Exercises and Stretches to Try

steps: Stand in Mountain Pose with your palms together; inhale and sweep your arms overhead, then exhale and fold forward, bending your knees as needed.
Inhale and step your right foot back into a low lunge, then step the left foot back to plank as you exhale.
Lower your knees, chest and chin to the mat, inhale and slide forward into Cobra, then exhale and press back to Downward-Facing Dog.
Inhale and step your right foot forward between your hands into a low lunge, exhale to bring the left foot forward and fold, then inhale up to standing.
Move with one breath per movement and lead with the left leg on the next round; drop your knees in plank for an easier version.
george:classical-sun-salutation.note: The alias 'Surya Namaskar C' is not used the same way everywhere. Some traditions use that name for a different sequence. Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Lie face down with your legs extended, tops of the feet on the mat, and hands under your shoulders with elbows tucked into your sides.
Inhale, press your pubic bone and feet into the mat and peel your chest forward and up using your back muscles, with only light pressure in your hands.
Feel a gentle stretch through your belly and chest while your lower and middle back muscles work.
Keep your elbows bent and shoulders away from your ears; hold for 3–5 breaths (15–30 seconds), then lower slowly as you exhale.
Don't push up onto straight arms or throw your head back; lift only as high as your lower back is comfortable.

references.title: Cobra Stretch (ACE Exercise Library)

george:cobra-pose.note: ACE's Cobra Stretch is the fitness version of the same prone back bend. This entry is the yoga Low Cobra, done with the elbows bent.

steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, a little wider than hip-width apart.
Let your knees fall inward to rest against each other so your legs can relax without effort.
Rest your hands on your belly or the floor and let your lower back settle naturally without pressing it down.
Breathe slowly for 3–5 minutes, feeling your back and hips soften with each exhale.
Put a folded blanket under your head if your chin tips up; to come out, roll onto one side and press up slowly.
george:constructive-rest-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Lie on your back with your legs extended and slightly apart and your arms a little away from your sides, palms facing up.
Let your feet fall open, close your eyes and allow the floor to take your full weight.
Scan your body from feet to head and soften your face, jaw, shoulders and belly.
Breathe naturally without controlling the breath and stay for 3–10 minutes.
Place a bolster or rolled blanket under your knees if your lower back feels tight; to finish, roll to one side and press up slowly.
george:corpse-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Stand with your feet very wide, about twice shoulder-width, toes pointing forward or slightly out.
Shift your weight to one side and sit your hips back and down into a squat on that leg, while the other leg straightens and its toes point up on the heel.
Keep the bent-leg heel flat and chest up; feel the stretch in the inner thigh of the straight leg and the work in the bent leg's glute and thigh.
Exhale as you push back up through the middle, then shift to the other side; alternate for the set reps.
Only go as low as you can with your heel down and back flat; put your hands on the floor or hold a support for balance.

references.title: Cossack Squat: 10 Benefits, Form Tips, Variations, Weights, More

steps: Kneel on a pad with your back to a couch or wall and slide one shin up it, the knee near the base and the top of the foot against it.
Step the other foot forward into a lunge with the foot flat and the knee over the ankle, hands on the front thigh or the floor.
Squeeze the glute of the back leg and tuck your pelvis slightly, then slowly lift your torso until you feel a strong stretch in the front of that thigh and hip.
Hold for 30–60 seconds while breathing slowly, then switch sides.
If it's too intense, keep your hands on the floor or move the back knee further from the wall, and ease off if your knee hurts.
george:couch-stretch.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out. Current steps were already correct.

steps: Sit or stand tall, reach your right arm up, then bend the elbow so your right hand drops between your shoulder blades.
Reach your left arm out to the side, turn it down, bend the elbow and slide the back of your left hand up your spine toward the right hand.
Hook your fingers together or hold a strap or towel between your hands, keeping the top elbow pointing up and your head upright.
Feel the stretch in the top arm's triceps and the front of the lower shoulder; breathe slowly and hold for 30–60 seconds, then switch arms.
Don't let your head push forward or your ribs flare out; use a strap instead of forcing your hands to meet.
george:cow-face-pose.note: This is the arms-only version. Full Gomukhasana also stacks the knees, one on top of the other, while seated. Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Sit on the floor with knees bent, feet flat about hip-width apart, and hands on the floor behind your hips with fingers pointing away from you.
Press through your feet and one hand to lift your hips, then reach your free arm up and over your head toward the side of your planted hand.
Open your chest toward the ceiling and squeeze your glutes; feel the stretch across the front of the reaching shoulder and chest.
Exhale as you reach and pause for a breath at the top, then lower your hips with control and alternate sides for the set reps.
Keep your neck relaxed and the supporting elbow straight but not locked; make the reach smaller if your shoulder or wrist pinches.
george:crab-reach.note: No reputable page found for 'crab reach' (only crab walk/crab hold). Steps follow the common crab reach-over drill. Web search limit was reached.

steps: Stand in Mountain Pose, sweep your arms overhead and interlace your fingers, keeping your index fingers pointing up.
Root through both feet and reach up through your fingertips, then lean your upper body over to one side.
Press your hips gently the other way to feel a long stretch down that whole side of your body, from hip to fingertips.
Breathe into the stretched side ribs for 3–5 breaths, then inhale back to centre and repeat on the other side.
Keep your chest facing forward instead of rolling it toward the floor, and keep your arms by your ears without squeezing your neck.
george:crescent-moon-pose.note: Some styles use the name 'Crescent Moon' for a lunge (Anjaneyasana). This entry is the standing side bend. Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Lie on your belly with your legs a comfortable distance apart and let your toes turn in or out, whichever relaxes your hips.
Fold your arms in front of you, stacking your hands or holding opposite elbows, and rest your forehead on them.
Breathe slowly into your belly and notice your lower back gently rise and fall with each breath.
Stay relaxed for 1–5 minutes, letting your shoulders, lower back and legs soften.
If your neck or lower back feels strained, slide your elbows farther forward or put a folded blanket under your chest; come out through Child's Pose.
george:crocodile-pose.note: Some traditions prop the chin on the hands with the elbows forward, which makes a mild back bend. Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Squat with your feet close together and knees wide, and plant your hands shoulder-width apart on the mat in front of you with fingers spread.
Bend your elbows back slightly and place your knees high on the backs of your upper arms, as close to your armpits as you can.
Lean forward to shift your weight into your hands, then lift one foot and then the other, drawing your heels toward your buttocks.
Feel your core, arms and wrists working; breathe steadily and hold for 5–20 seconds, then lower your feet with control.
Look slightly ahead instead of straight down and keep a cushion in front of your face while learning; practise lifting one foot at a time first.
george:crow-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Stand on your left leg, bend your right knee and hold the inside of your right foot or ankle with your right hand.
Reach your left arm forward and up, then press your right foot back into your hand as you tip your chest slightly forward.
Let the lifted leg rise behind you with your hips square, feeling a stretch through the front of the thigh, hip and shoulder.
Breathe steadily and hold for 5–8 breaths (about 20–30 seconds), then lower slowly and switch sides.
Keep the standing knee soft rather than locked and the lifted knee from swinging out to the side; rest your front hand on a wall for balance.
george:dancers-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Step your feet wide, turn your front foot forward and bend that knee over the ankle into Warrior II, with your arms reaching out at shoulder height.
Inhale and tip back into Reverse Warrior, sliding your back hand down the back leg and reaching your front arm up and overhead.
Exhale and lower your front forearm to your thigh, or your hand to a block, into Extended Side Angle, reaching your top arm over your ear.
Flow between the shapes with your breath for 5–8 rounds, feeling your legs work and your sides stretch, then switch sides.
Keep your front knee bent over the ankle the whole time instead of letting it fall inward, and shorten your stance if your hips or knees complain.
george:dancing-warrior-flow.note: 'Dancing Warrior' is a loose name. Other sequences with this name use different poses. Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Stand under a sturdy pull-up bar, using a step or box if needed, and grip it overhand with hands about shoulder-width apart.
Step off or bend your knees so you hang on straight arms, letting your body lengthen from your hands down through your lats and armpits.
Keep your grip firm and your core lightly braced, and let your shoulders relax upward for a passive stretch through the lats, shoulders and forearms.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time, starting around 10-20 seconds and building toward a minute.
Step back onto the box before letting go rather than dropping; keep your toes on the box to take some weight, and stop if you feel sharp shoulder pain.

references.title: Dead Hang: Benefits, How to, for Pullup, Variations, and More

steps: Stand facing a sturdy desk, counter or chair back and rest your hands on its edge, shoulder-width apart.
Walk your feet back and hinge at your hips, arms straight, until your back is flat and your arms line up beside your ears.
Let your chest sink gently toward the floor and push your hips back to feel the stretch under your arms and along the sides of your back.
Breathe slowly into your ribs and hold for the set time, sinking a little deeper each time you breathe out.
Soften your knees if your hamstrings pull, and avoid rounding your lower back or letting your head drop below your arms.

references.title: Golf stretches for a more fluid swing - Mayo Clinic

george:desk-lat-stretch.note: Mayo Clinic page describes the same move as a standing back stretch holding the back of a bench or chair.

steps: Start on your hands and knees, then lower onto your forearms with your elbows under your shoulders and your forearms parallel or hands clasped.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back into an inverted V, like Downward-Facing Dog on your forearms.
Press your forearms down and lift your shoulders away from the floor, letting your chest move toward your thighs.
Feel your shoulders working and a stretch through your hamstrings, calves and upper back; breathe steadily for 5–10 breaths.
Bend your knees if your back rounds, keep your head off the floor and don't let your elbows slide wider than your shoulders.
george:dolphin-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Stand facing a door frame or sturdy post with your feet close to its base and grip it with both hands at about hip to chest height.
Sit your hips back and shift them out to one side, letting your arms straighten so your body curves into a long C shape.
Feel the stretch along the side your hips push toward, from the hip up through the side of your back to the armpit.
Breathe deeply into that side and hold for the set time, then shift your hips the other way to stretch the other side.
Keep your back long instead of rounding to reach lower; gripping higher on the frame moves the stretch toward your upper back.

references.title: Latissimus dorsi stretch door (Shoulder extensors latissimus dorsi stretch, with side bending, hands on rail, standing)

george:doorframe-lat-stretch.note: Only a physio exercise-video platform (Physitrack) was found for this exact variant; no preferred-site page.

steps: Stand in a doorway and place one forearm and palm flat on the frame, elbow bent about 90 degrees and level with or just below your shoulder.
Take a small step forward through the doorway and gently turn your chest away from that arm until you feel a stretch across your chest and front of the shoulder.
Keep your shoulder blade drawn back and down, and don't let the shoulder roll forward or shrug toward your ear.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time, easing a little deeper as you breathe out without bouncing, then switch arms.
Raise the elbow slightly to target the lower chest or lower it for the upper chest, and back off if you feel tingling or pinching in the shoulder.

references.title: 5 Chest Stretch Variations to Improve Flexibility
Stretches and Exercises To Improve Poor Posture

steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold a dowel upright along your back, one hand behind your neck and one at your lower back, touching your head, upper back and tailbone.
Unlock your knees slightly and push your hips straight back, letting your torso tip forward while all three points stay on the stick.
Stop when you feel your hamstrings tighten or the stick starts to leave a contact point, especially your tailbone.
Breathe in as you hinge, then exhale, squeeze your glutes and drive your hips forward to stand tall; repeat for the set reps.
Do not turn it into a squat by bending your knees a lot; if the stick leaves your tailbone, your lower back is rounding.

references.title: Two Classic Exercises Everyone Should Master

steps: Start in Downward-Facing Dog with hands shoulder-width apart, feet hip-width apart, hips lifted high and spine long.
Bend one knee and lift that heel while you press the other heel toward the floor and straighten that leg.
Feel the stretch in the calf and back of the straight leg, then switch legs smoothly in a pedalling rhythm.
Breathe steadily and pause briefly as each heel sinks; each heel press counts as one rep.
Keep your hips level and spine long; it is fine if your heels do not reach the floor, and bend both knees slightly if your back rounds.

references.title: 20 Ways to Change Up Your Down Dog
Calves Feeling Tight? These 8 Yoga Poses Can Help Loosen Up Your Legs.

steps: Start on your hands and knees with your hands slightly ahead of your shoulders and knees under your hips, then tuck your toes.
Exhale and lift your hips up and back so your body forms an inverted V, spreading your fingers and pressing through your whole hand.
Lengthen your spine first, bending your knees as much as needed, then work your heels toward the floor to stretch your hamstrings and calves.
Let your head hang between your upper arms and breathe slowly for 5–10 breaths (30–60 seconds).
Don't round your back just to straighten your legs or sink into your shoulders; push the floor away and keep a knee bend if needed.

references.title: Yoga Poses 101: How To Do a Downward Dog Pose

george:downward-facing-dog.note: The search result URL had a '&gsessionid=...' tracking suffix, which has been removed.

steps: Sit or stand tall and reach both arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height.
Cross one arm over the other at the elbows, bend both elbows and wrap your forearms so your palms (or the backs of your hands) touch.
Lift your elbows to shoulder height and press your forearms gently forward, away from your face, to feel a stretch between your shoulder blades and in the upper back.
Breathe slowly into your upper back and hold for the set time, then unwind and repeat with the other arm on top.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears; if your hands can't meet, hold a strap between them or simply hug your hands to opposite shoulders.

references.title: Eagle Pose: How to Practice Garudasana - Yoga Journal
Eagle Pose Variations: 4 Ways to Make Garudasana More Comfy

steps: Stand with knees slightly bent, shift onto your left foot and cross your right thigh over your left, hooking your right foot behind your left calf if you can.
Reach your arms forward, cross your left arm over your right at the elbows, bend them and bring your palms or the backs of your hands together.
Lift your elbows to shoulder height and move them away from your face, feeling a stretch between your shoulder blades and in the outer hip.
Sink your hips a little lower and breathe steadily for 5–8 breaths, then unwind and switch sides.
For easier balance, rest the toes of the crossed leg on the floor instead of hooking the calf, and hold opposite shoulders if your palms won't meet.
george:eagle-pose.note: In the classical pose, the arm on top is on the opposite side to the leg on top. Some teachers cross the same side. Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Sit on the edge of a folded blanket and cross your shins, sliding each foot beneath the opposite knee.
Let your knees relax down toward the floor and stack your shoulders over your hips to lengthen your spine.
Rest your hands on your knees or thighs, soften your shoulders and face, and notice a gentle opening in your hips.
Breathe slowly and stay for 1–5 minutes, then cross your shins the other way next time.
If your knees sit higher than your hips or your back rounds, sit on a higher blanket or support your knees on blocks.
george:easy-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Sit in Easy Pose on a folded blanket with your shins crossed and your spine tall.
Inhale to lengthen, then exhale and walk your hands forward along the floor, folding from your hips.
Let your torso drape forward and rest your forehead on the floor or a block, feeling the stretch in your outer hips, glutes and back.
Breathe slowly for 1–2 minutes, then walk your hands back up, cross your legs the other way and repeat.
Keep both sitting bones on the blanket; if your knees or hips feel strained, fold less and rest your head on a block or bolster.
george:easy-pose-forward-fold.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Kneel with your big toes touching and knees about mat-width apart, then sit your hips back toward your heels.
Walk your hands forward and lower your chest between your thighs, resting your forehead on the mat or a block.
Reach actively through your fingertips to feel a stretch along your lats, sides and lower back, then soften your shoulders.
Breathe slowly into your back for 30 seconds to 2 minutes.
If your hips don't reach your heels, place a folded blanket between them or under your knees.
george:extended-childs-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Stand tall on your left leg, put your left hand on your hip and draw your right knee up toward your chest.
Hook your right big toe with your right index and middle fingers, or loop a strap around the ball of that foot.
Slowly straighten the right leg forward as far as you can while keeping your chest lifted and hips level, feeling the stretch in the back of the leg.
Breathe steadily and hold for 5–8 breaths (about 20–30 seconds), then release and switch legs.
Keep the knee bent, or hold the knee instead of the toe, if your back starts to round; stand near a wall for balance.
george:extended-hand-to-big-toe-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: From Warrior II with your right knee bent over the ankle, lower your right forearm onto your right thigh, or your right hand to a block outside the foot.
Sweep your left arm over your ear so there is one long line from your back heel to your fingertips.
Press your front knee toward the little-toe side and turn your chest toward the ceiling, feeling the stretch along your top side and inner thighs.
Breathe steadily for 5–8 breaths, then inhale back to Warrior II and switch sides.
Don't sink your weight into the front arm or let the front knee drift inward; keep your forearm on your thigh until you can go lower easily.
george:extended-side-angle-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Sit or stand with your elbows bent and hands up in front of you, wrists straight and fingers straight and together.
Move slowly through four shapes: hook fist (bend the middle and end joints), full fist, tabletop (bend only at the big knuckles), and straight fist (fingertips at the base of the palm).
Return to straight fingers between shapes; you should feel the fingers and front of the forearm move smoothly, without pain.
Hold each shape for about 3 seconds while breathing normally; one pass through all the shapes is one rep.
Do not force a shape that hurts; stay in a comfortable range, especially after a hand injury or surgery.

references.title: 16 Hand and Wrist Exercises To Help Ease Arthritis Pain

steps: Sit tall on a folded blanket with your knees bent and place your left shin parallel to the front edge of the mat.
Stack your right shin on top so the right ankle rests just past the left knee and the right knee sits over the left ankle, both feet flexed.
Fill any gap under the top knee with a block or blanket, then hinge forward from your hips if you want more stretch.
Feel the stretch in your outer hips and glutes; breathe slowly and hold for 30 seconds to 2 minutes, then switch which shin is on top.
Back off right away if you feel pressure in your knees, and sit cross-legged instead if you can't stack your shins.
george:fire-log-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight and together, and slide your hands palms down under your buttocks with your elbows close to your sides.
Press into your forearms and elbows to lift your chest, then lightly rest the crown of your head on the floor, keeping most of your weight in your arms.
Lift through your breastbone to feel the stretch across your chest, the fronts of your shoulders and your throat.
Breathe steadily for 3–5 breaths (15–30 seconds), then press into your forearms, lift your head and lower your back down.
Don't put much weight on your neck; for a gentler version, lie back over a block or bolster under your upper back with your head on the floor.
george:fish-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Hold one arm out in front of you, elbow straight and thumb pointing up, then tuck your thumb into your palm and wrap your fingers gently over it.
Slowly bend your wrist down toward the little-finger side until you feel a stretch along the thumb side of your wrist and lower forearm.
Use your other hand to add light pressure only if you need more, keeping the stretch mild.
Breathe normally and hold for the set time (about 15-30 seconds), then release and repeat with the other hand.
This position can feel sharp if the thumb tendons are irritated, so ease off straight away if you feel pain rather than a gentle pull.

references.title: De Quervain's Disease: Exercises
De Quervain's Disease: Exercises

george:fist-tuck-wrist-stretch.note: This is the Finkelstein stretch position (also used as a test for de Quervain's tenosynovitis), so keep it gentle.

steps: Sit on the end of a foam roller and lie back along it so it supports your head and spine from tailbone to skull, knees bent and feet flat.
Let your arms fall out to the sides in a T with palms facing up, or slightly higher in a goalpost shape.
Relax and let gravity gently open your chest and the front of your shoulders; it should feel like a mild stretch, not a strain.
Breathe slowly and deeply into your chest and stay for the set time, anywhere from 30 seconds to a few minutes.
If your hands tingle or your shoulders pinch, move your arms closer to your sides or bend your elbows.

references.title: Supine Foam Roller Chest Stretch
Foam rolling: how-to moves (Healthline)

george:foam-roller-chest-opener.note: Healthline page title was shown oddly in search ('Feeling the burn'); it describes lying lengthwise on the roller with arms in a T.

steps: Lie on your back with a foam roller across your upper back just below your shoulder blades, knees bent, feet flat and hands behind your head with elbows in.
Keep your hips on the floor and ribs down, then gently arch your upper back over the roller, letting your head follow without pulling on your neck.
Feel a stretch through your mid-back; pause, return to the start, then shift the roller up a few centimetres to work the next segment.
Exhale as you extend and do a few reps at each spot for the set reps.
Do not let your lower back arch or roll onto your lower back or neck; lift your hips briefly only to reposition.

references.title: Thoracic Mobility Exercises to Address Shoulder Pain

steps: Sit at a table and rest your forearm palm-down on a tennis or massage ball placed just below your elbow.
Lean gently into the ball and roll slowly toward your wrist and back, then turn your palm up to work the inner forearm.
You should feel firm but tolerable pressure in the forearm muscles; on a tender spot, pause and slowly open and close your hand.
Breathe slowly and hold tender spots for 15 to 30 seconds for the set time, then switch arms.
Keep the pressure moderate and stay off the bony point of the elbow and the inside of the wrist.

references.title: Forearm Tendonitis: Symptoms, Treatment, Recovery, and More

steps: Start in Plank Pose with your hands under your shoulders, your body in one straight line and your core engaged.
Shift forward onto the balls of your feet so your shoulders move slightly ahead of your wrists.
Exhale and bend your elbows straight back, hugging them to your ribs, and lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Feel your triceps, chest and core working; keep your shoulders level with your elbows and hold for 1–2 breaths before moving on.
Lower your knees to the mat first if you can't keep your hips in line with your shoulders, and don't let your shoulders dip below your elbows.
george:four-limbed-staff-pose.note: Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Start on your hands and knees on a padded mat, then slowly slide your knees out wide, keeping your ankles in line with your knees and feet flexed.
Lower onto your forearms and let your hips sink gently back toward your heels.
Feel a deep stretch along your inner thighs and groin, with your shins parallel to each other.
Breathe slowly and hold for 1–3 minutes, keeping your lower back long instead of letting it sag.
Ease in gradually and stop at a strong but tolerable stretch; to come out, shift forward and walk your knees back together.
george:frog-pose.note: This is the Yin-style wide-knee frog. The Sanskrit alias is ambiguous: Mandukasana is a seated pose in some traditions, and Bhekasana is a face-down quad stretch. Search budget ran out before this entry could be checked; steps are written from standard technique and still need a source.

steps: Start on hands and knees on a padded mat, then slide your knees wide with shins parallel, ankles in line with knees and the inner edges of your feet on the floor.
Keep your spine neutral and slowly rock your hips back toward your heels until you feel a stretch in your inner thighs.
Pause for a second at the end of the range as you exhale, then rock forward to the start.
Repeat smoothly for the set reps, letting the range increase gradually.
Do not force your knees wider or let your lower back round; bring your knees closer together if it feels too intense.

references.title: Frog Pose Benefits: How to Get the Most from Mandukasana

george:frog-rocks.note: Source shows the static Frog Pose; the rocking version moves in and out of the same position.

steps: Stand with your feet a little wider than your hips and turn your toes out slightly.
Bend your knees and lower your hips into a deep squat, letting your knees open wider than your torso; rest your heels on a folded blanket if they lift.
Press your palms together at your chest and use your elbows to gently widen your knees while you lengthen your spine upward.
Feel the stretch in your inner thighs, hips and ankles; breathe slowly and hold for 5–10 breaths.
Sit on a block if the squat is too deep, and come out if you feel any pain in your knees.

references.title: Malasana (Garland Pose or Squat)
Garland Pose (Malasana) Cues - Yoga Video

steps: Kneel upright on a padded mat with your hips over your knees, then stretch one leg out to the side in line with the kneeling knee, foot flat on the floor.
Rest the hand on that side on the straight leg and, as you inhale, sweep your other arm up beside your ear.
Exhale and bend sideways over the straight leg, sliding your hand down the leg as your top arm reaches over your head.
Feel the stretch along the side of your body from hip to fingertips and in the inner thigh of the straight leg; hold for 5–8 breaths, then switch sides.
Keep your chest turned forward instead of collapsing toward the floor, and pad the kneeling knee or do it seated on a chair if kneeling hurts.

references.title: Gate Pose (Parighasana)
Stretch Your Side Body in Gate Pose (Parighasana)

steps: Stand with your feet about three to four feet apart and turn your toes out about 45 degrees.
Bend your knees and lower your hips toward knee height, keeping your knees moving in the same direction as your toes.
Lift your arms into a goalpost shape with elbows bent, or press your palms together at your chest, keeping your torso upright and tailbone pointing down.
Feel your thighs and glutes working and a stretch in your inner thighs; breathe steadily and hold for 5–8 breaths.
Avoid leaning forward or letting your knees cave inward; squat less deeply or practise with your back against a wall if they do.

references.title: Goddess Squat Pose (Utkata Konasana): Steps & Benefits

steps: Kneel on one knee, padded if needed, and extend the other leg straight out to the side with the foot flat and toes pointing forward.
Place your hands on the floor in front of you or on your thighs and keep your back flat.
Slowly shift your hips back toward the heel of the kneeling leg until you feel a stretch along the inner thigh of the straight leg.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time, easing a little deeper as you breathe out, then switch legs.
Keep the straight knee facing forward rather than rolling in and don't round your back; shift back less or soften the knee to make it easier.
george:half-kneeling-adductor-stretch.note: No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Kneel on one knee on a pad with the other foot flat in front, both knees bent about 90 degrees and torso upright.
Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg and tuck your tailbone slightly so your pelvis is level.
Rock your hips forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the kneeling hip and thigh, pause for a second, then rock back.
Exhale as you rock forward; do the set reps, then switch legs.
Keep your ribs down and do not arch your lower back to go further; a small rock with a tucked pelvis works better.

references.title: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch

george:half-kneeling-hip-flexor-rocks.note: Source shows the static kneeling hip flexor stretch; the rocks are the dynamic version of the same position.

steps: Sit tall on the mat or a folded blanket with your legs straight out in front of you.
Bend one knee and place that foot on the floor outside the opposite knee, then fold the bottom leg so its heel rests near the opposite hip, or keep it straight.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, then exhale and turn toward the bent knee, hooking the opposite elbow outside it and placing your other hand on the floor behind you.
Feel the twist through your middle back and the outer hip of the top leg; lengthen on each inhale and turn a little more on each exhale for 5–8 breaths.
Don't lever the twist with your arm or strain your neck; hug the knee instead of hooking the elbow if your shoulders are tight, then switch sides.

references.title: Half Lord of the Fishes Pose (Ardha Matsyendrasana)
Cues for Half Lord of the Fishes Pose (Ardha Matsyendrasana)

steps: Sit cross-legged on a folded blanket so your hips are a little higher than your knees.
Hold one foot with both hands and lift it onto the opposite thigh close to the hip crease, sole turned up, letting the rotation come from your hip rather than your knee.
Tuck your other foot under the opposite knee and sit tall with your hands resting on your knees.
Feel a stretch in the outer hip and front of the lifted leg; breathe slowly and hold for 1–2 minutes.
Come out at once if your knee hurts, put a folded blanket under any lifted knee, and switch which foot is on top each time you practise.

references.title: Half Lotus Pose - Yoga Basics

steps: Start in Triangle Pose, then bend your front knee and place your front fingertips on the floor or a block about a foot ahead of and slightly outside your front foot.
Shift your weight into the front foot and straighten that leg as you lift your back leg until it is level with your hip, foot flexed and toes facing sideways.
Stack your top hip over the bottom one, open your chest to the side and reach your top arm toward the ceiling.
Feel your standing leg, the outer hip of the lifted leg and your core working; breathe steadily for about 5 breaths, then lower with control and switch sides.
Keep a slight bend in the standing knee, look down if balancing is hard, or practise with your back against a wall.

references.title: Half Moon Pose: How to Practice Ardha Chandrasana
Get Grounded and Practice Balance In Half Moon Pose (Arda Chandrasana)

steps: Start in a low lunge with your back knee on a padded mat and your hands on the floor or blocks either side of your front foot.
Shift your hips back until they are over your back knee and straighten your front leg, flexing the front foot so the toes point up.
Keep your spine long and hinge forward from your hips until you feel a stretch along the back of the front thigh and calf.
Breathe slowly and hold for 5–10 breaths, then switch sides.
Keep your hips level and stacked over the back knee; bend the front knee slightly or raise your hands on blocks if your back starts to round.

references.title: 4 Common Misalignments in Half Splits (And How to Correct Them)

steps: From a standing forward fold with feet hip-width apart, place your hands on your shins or your fingertips on the floor or blocks.
Inhale and lift your chest forward, hinging from your hips, until your back is long and flat and roughly parallel to the floor.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears and look at the floor just ahead of your toes, keeping the back of your neck long.
Feel your hamstrings stretch and your back muscles working; hold for a few breaths, or move between this and the fold with your breath.
Bend your knees as much as you need to stop your back rounding, and keep your head down if you have a neck injury.

references.title: Standing Half Forward Bend (Ardha Uttanasana)

steps: Stand in Mountain Pose with your feet hip-width apart and your arms by your sides.
Inhale as you sweep your arms out and overhead, then exhale and fold forward from your hips, bending your knees as needed.
Inhale to a half lift with a flat back and hands on your shins, then exhale back into the fold.
Inhale to rise all the way up with your arms overhead and exhale your hands to your chest, feeling your hamstrings and back lengthen.
Move slowly with one breath per movement and repeat rounds for the set time; keep your knees soft rather than locked in the folds.

references.title: Half Sun Salutation • Yoga Basics

george:half-sun-salutation.note: A flowing sequence rather than a single held pose; 'time' here means repeating rounds for the duration.

steps: Stand tall, then step one foot slightly forward onto its heel with the toes up and that leg straight, back knee soft.
Hinge at your hips with a flat back and sweep both hands down and forward past the front foot in a scooping motion.
Feel a light stretch behind the front thigh and calf, then rise, step forward and repeat on the other leg.
Exhale as you sweep down and keep a smooth walking rhythm for the set reps per leg.
Do not round your back or bounce to reach the floor; reaching only to your shin is fine.

references.title: Dynamic Warm-Ups for Runners and Lifters

george:hamstring-sweeps.note: Source lists the jogging version ('Jog Scoops'); the walking sweep is the same scooping hamstring drill.

steps: Sit or stand tall and lightly lace your fingers behind your head with your elbows pointing forward.
Breathe in as you open your elbows wide and draw them back, squeezing your shoulder blades together and lifting your chest.
Feel the stretch across your chest and the front of your shoulders.
Hold the open position for the set time, breathing slowly and easing the elbows slightly further back as you breathe out.
Keep your chin level and avoid pulling your head forward with your hands or arching your lower back.
george:hands-behind-head-chest-opener.note: A Mayo Clinic search summary described this exact stretch, but the specific page could not be pinned down. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Lie on your back and draw your knees in toward your belly.
Open your knees a little wider than your torso, bringing them toward your armpits, and hold the outer edges of your feet, your ankles or your shins.
Stack your ankles over your knees so your shins point straight up, then gently pull down while pressing your feet up into your hands.
Feel the stretch in your inner thighs, groin and lower back; keep your head and tailbone on the mat and breathe slowly for 30–60 seconds.
Loop a strap around each foot or hold your shins if you can't reach your feet, and rock gently side to side if it feels good.

references.title: Happy Baby Pose: How to Practice Ananda Balasana

steps: Sit on a folded blanket with both legs straight, then bend one knee and rest that foot against the inner thigh of the straight leg, letting the bent knee drop out.
Turn your chest to face the straight leg and inhale to sit tall.
Exhale and fold forward from your hips over the straight leg, holding your shin, your ankle or a strap around the foot.
Feel the stretch along the back of the straight leg and your lower back; lengthen on each inhale and fold a little deeper on each exhale for 5–10 breaths, then switch sides.
Lead with your chest instead of rounding to pull your head toward your knee, and move the bent knee closer to the straight leg if it feels strained.

references.title: Head-to-Knee Forward Bend (Janu Sirsasana)
Head-to-Knee Pose (Janu Sirsasana)

steps: Kneel on a padded mat with your knees together and your feet slightly wider than your hips, tops of the feet flat and toes pointing straight back.
As you sit back, use your thumbs to ease your calves slightly outward and lower your hips onto the floor between your heels, or onto a block if they don't reach.
Sit tall with your hands resting on your thighs and your shoulders relaxed.
Feel the stretch along the front of your thighs and ankles; breathe evenly and hold for 30 seconds to a few minutes.
Raise your seat with blocks or blankets until your knees feel no strain, and come out immediately if you feel knee pain.

references.title: Hero Pose: How to Practice Virasana
Master Hero Pose (Virasana) in 5 Steps

steps: From standing or Downward-Facing Dog, step one foot forward so the front knee is over the ankle and the back heel is lifted, feet about hip-width apart.
Inhale and lift your torso upright, reaching your arms overhead with your palms facing each other.
Straighten the back leg by pressing back through the heel, draw your tailbone gently down and keep your hips facing forward.
Feel your front thigh and glutes working and a stretch at the front of the back hip; breathe steadily for 30 seconds to a minute, then switch sides.
Don't let the front knee drift past the ankle or your lower back arch; keep your hands on your hips or the back knee down if balance is hard.

references.title: High Lunge: How to Practice the Yoga Pose
High Lunge, Crescent Variation

steps: Stand on one leg with a soft knee, holding a wall or rack lightly, and hinge forward until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, free leg reaching back.
Keeping the standing knee and foot still, rotate your pelvis open so the free hip turns up toward the ceiling.
Rotate back and close your pelvis down toward the standing leg; you should feel the glute and outer hip of the standing leg working hard.
Breathe steadily and move slowly through the set reps, then switch legs.
Turn from the hip rather than twisting your lower back; use more hand support or a smaller range if you wobble.
george:hip-airplane.note: Common rehab/mobility drill; web search limit was reached before a source could be verified.

steps: Stand tall on one leg holding a wall or rack, and brace your core and glutes so your pelvis and torso stay still.
Lift the free knee in front of you as high as you can, then open it out to the side.
Keep circling by turning the knee back behind you as if stepping over a hurdle, then bring the thigh down beside the standing leg; feel the deep hip muscles working.
Move as slowly as you can and breathe normally; do the set reps in one direction, reverse the circle, then switch legs.
Do not tilt or twist your torso to make the circle bigger; a smaller, controlled circle is the goal.
george:hip-cars.note: Also commonly done on hands and knees. Web search limit was reached before a source could be verified.

steps: Start in Warrior I with your front knee bent over the ankle and your back foot flat, angled slightly out.
Interlace your fingers behind your back, or hold a strap between your hands, and straighten your arms to open your chest.
Exhale and bow your torso forward to the inside of the front knee, letting your clasped hands lift up and over toward your head.
Feel the stretch across your shoulders, chest and the front of the back hip while your front leg works; breathe for 4–8 breaths.
Keep the front knee over the ankle rather than letting it fall inward, use a strap if your hands won't meet, then inhale to rise slowly and switch sides.

references.title: The 5 Warrior Poses of Yoga • Yoga Basics

george:humble-warrior.note: Most teachers build it from Warrior I legs (hips forward); Yoga Basics describes Warrior II legs (hips to the side). Steps use the Warrior I version.

steps: Lie on your back with both legs straight, or bend the resting knee with that foot flat if your lower back prefers.
Bend one knee toward your chest and hold it with both hands, one on the knee and one at the ankle.
Gently draw the knee across your body toward the opposite shoulder until you feel a stretch deep in the buttock and outer hip.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time (about 20-30 seconds), then lower the leg and switch sides.
Keep your hips and shoulders flat and pull only to a comfortable stretch; ease off if you feel pinching at the front of the hip.
george:knee-to-opposite-shoulder-stretch.note: No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Stand facing a wall in a split stance with your front toes a few centimetres from the wall and your hands on it for balance.
Keeping your front heel down, bend the front knee and drive it forward over your middle toes until it touches the wall.
You should feel a stretch in the calf or a gentle bend at the front of the ankle; return and repeat for the set reps.
Breathe normally; when touching the wall is easy, move your foot back a little, then switch legs after the set.
Do not let your heel lift, your arch collapse or your knee cave inward.
george:knee-to-wall-ankle-mobilization.note: Well-known drill (based on the knee-to-wall test); web search limit was reached before a source could be verified.

steps: Kneel facing a bench, sturdy chair seat or couch and rest your elbows on its edge, shoulder-width apart, with palms together.
Sit your hips back toward your heels and let your chest and head sink down between your arms toward the floor.
Feel the stretch along the sides of your back, under your arms and into the backs of your upper arms.
Breathe deeply and hold for the set time, letting your chest drop a little more each time you breathe out.
For a deeper stretch, bend your elbows to bring your hands behind your head; avoid arching your lower back, and pad your knees if needed.

references.title: Exercise Library: Kneeling Lat Stretch (w/bench)
Lat Stretches: 10 Exercises to Strengthen, Support, and Prevent Injury

george:kneeling-lat-stretch.note: ACE page matches by title; Healthline page covers a close kneeling variation with the arm resting on a chair or ball.

steps: Kneel on a mat with your knees together, the tops of your feet flat on the floor and toes pointing straight back.
Sit your hips back onto your heels, placing your hands on the floor beside your knees or slightly behind you for support.
To go deeper, lean back onto your hands and lift your knees a little off the floor until you feel a stretch along the front of your shins and ankles.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time.
Put a folded towel under your ankles or sit on a block if it's too intense, and skip the knee lift if your knees complain.
george:kneeling-shin-stretch.note: ACE has an exercise-library entry 'Kneeling TA Stretch' (https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/195/kneeling-ta-stretch/) that may be this stretch, but its content could not be confirmed, so it is not listed. No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.
