steps: Kneel with your knees together and tuck your toes under so you rest on the balls of your feet, heels pointing up.
Slowly sit your hips back toward your heels, using your hands on the floor or thighs to control how much weight goes onto your feet.
Feel the stretch along the soles of your feet and under your toes.
Breathe slowly and start with short holds, building up to the set time as your feet get used to it.
Lean forward onto your hands to lighten it, and make sure all your toes, including the little ones, are tucked under rather than rolled out.
george:kneeling-toe-stretch.note: No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Kneel on a mat and place the backs of your hands on the floor in front of your knees, fingers pointing toward you.
Keeping your elbows straight, slowly shift your weight back until you feel a stretch along the top of your forearms and wrists.
Lean back only slightly at first, as this stretch gets intense quickly.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time, then shake out your hands.
Keep the backs of your hands flat; move them closer to your knees or do one hand at a time to make it easier.
george:kneeling-wrist-extensor-stretch.note: No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Start in Plank Pose with your hands under your shoulders, then lower both knees to the mat.
Keeping your hips lifted, bend your elbows straight back close to your ribs and lower your chest and chin to the floor between your hands.
In the final shape your toes, knees, chest, chin and hands touch the mat while your hips stay high, with a gentle bend in your upper back.
Feel your arms, chest and shoulders working; hold for a few breaths, or move through it on an exhale and slide forward into Cobra.
Lower slowly instead of dropping, keep your elbows hugging in, and come out if your lower back or shoulders feel pinched.

references.title: Eight-Limbed Pose - Yoga Basics

steps: Sit sideways with one hip close to a wall, with a folded blanket nearby if you want it under your hips.
Lie back and swing your legs up the wall, then shuffle your hips close to it, or a little further away if your hamstrings are tight.
Rest your arms by your sides, palms up, and let your legs relax; you may feel a mild stretch in the back of your legs.
Close your eyes and breathe slowly for 5–15 minutes.
If your lower back strains, rest your calves on a chair instead; to come out, bend your knees, roll to one side and pause before sitting up.

references.title: Legs Up the Wall Pose: How to Practice Viparita Karani
Relieve Stress with Legs-up-the-Wall Pose (Viparita Karani) - Yoga Journal

steps: Sit tall and hold the edge of your chair seat with one hand to anchor that shoulder down.
Turn your head about 45 degrees away from the anchored side and tip your chin down, as if bringing your nose toward your opposite armpit.
Rest your free hand on the back of your head and add very light pressure until you feel a stretch from your neck to the top of your shoulder blade.
Breathe slowly and hold for the set time (about 20-30 seconds), then switch sides.
Keep the anchored shoulder down and never yank your head; you can skip the hand and let the weight of your head do the work.
george:levator-scapulae-stretch.note: No reference: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps written from general knowledge.

steps: Start in a low lunge with one foot forward between your hands and your back knee on a padded mat.
Walk your front foot toward the edge of the mat and bring both hands to the inside of that foot, toes pointing forward.
Let your hips sink forward and down, staying on your hands or lowering to your forearms on blocks or the floor if your hips allow.
Feel the stretch in your inner thigh, groin and the front of the back hip; breathe slowly for 5–10 breaths, then switch sides.
Keep the front knee pointing over the toes instead of collapsing inward, and stay on your hands or blocks rather than forcing your forearms down.
george:lizard-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Lie face down with your arms by your sides, palms down and forehead on the mat; a folded blanket under your hips adds comfort.
Press the tops of your feet down, then on an inhale lift your head, chest, arms and legs off the floor together.
Reach back through your fingertips and toes, keeping your gaze down and the back of your neck long.
Feel your back muscles, glutes and hamstrings working; breathe steadily for 3–5 breaths, then lower with control on an exhale.
For an easier version lift only your chest or only your legs, and avoid jutting your chin forward.
george:locust-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: From a lunge, lower your back knee onto a padded mat with the top of the back foot down, and stack your front knee over the ankle.
Inhale and lift your torso upright, raising your arms overhead or resting your hands on your front thigh.
Draw your tailbone gently down and let your hips sink forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the back hip and thigh.
Breathe steadily and hold for 30 seconds to a minute, then switch sides.
Don't arch your lower back to go deeper, and keep your hands on blocks beside the front foot if balance is hard.
george:low-lunge.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat and together, and arms out to the sides on the floor.
Keeping your knees together and shoulders down, slowly lower both knees to one side as far as is comfortable.
Feel a gentle stretch in your lower back and the side of your hip, then use your abs to bring the knees back through the centre and over to the other side.
Exhale as the knees lower and inhale as they return; each side counts as one rep.
Do not let the opposite shoulder lift or force the knees to the floor; move only in a pain-free range.
george:lower-trunk-rotations.note: Standard low-back mobility exercise; web search limit was reached before a source could be verified.

steps: Sit tall with both legs straight in front of you, then bend one knee and place that foot flat near the same-side sitting bone, a hand's width from the other thigh.
Lean forward and reach the arm on the bent-knee side inside that shin, then wrap it around the shin and behind your back.
Reach your other arm behind you to clasp hands or a strap, inhale to lengthen, then exhale and fold forward over the straight leg.
Feel the stretch in the hamstrings of the straight leg, your back and the front of your shoulders; hold for 5–8 breaths, then switch sides.
Keep the bent knee pointing up and lead with your chest; hold the shin instead of binding if your shoulders are tight.

references.title: Marichyasana I Master Class with Colleen Sandman Yee + Rodney Yee

steps: Begin in Half Splits with your back knee padded and blocks under your hands either side of your front leg.
Slowly slide the front heel forward and the back knee back, lowering your hips only as far as you can stay in control.
Keep both hips facing forward and place a bolster or block under the front thigh for support.
Feel the stretch along the back of the front leg and the front of the back hip; breathe slowly for 5–10 breaths.
Never bounce or force the last part of the range; come out by bending the front knee and sliding back, then switch sides.

references.title: Hanuman’s Pose (Full Splits)
5 Hanumanasana Variations to Empower Your Practice

steps: Stand in Mountain Pose, inhale your arms overhead with palms together, and lean into a side bend (Crescent Moon) to each side.
Step your feet wide and bend into Goddess Pose, then straighten your legs into Star Pose with your arms out wide.
Turn to one side through Triangle and Pyramid, lower into a low lunge, then shift sideways into a deep side lunge.
Pass through a Garland Pose squat in the middle, then repeat side lunge, low lunge, Pyramid, Triangle, Star, Goddess and Crescent Moon on the other side.
Move slowly with one breath per pose, feeling your side body, hips and legs stretch, and stay higher in the squats if your knees complain.

references.title: Celebrate the Solar Eclipse with This Moon Salutation

george:moon-salutation.note: The order of poses in a Moon Salutation differs between traditions; steps follow the common Kripalu-style circle. Only one partly confirmed source.

steps: Stand with your feet together or hip-width apart, toes forward and your weight spread evenly across your heels and the balls of your feet.
Gently firm your thighs, lengthen your tailbone toward the floor and stack your ribs over your pelvis without locking your knees.
Roll your shoulders back and down, let your arms hang by your sides with palms facing forward, and lengthen up through the crown of your head.
Feel your legs and core lightly engaged while your shoulders relax; breathe evenly and hold still for 5–10 breaths.
Avoid pushing your hips forward or arching your lower back, and stand with your feet hip-width apart if balance feels shaky.

references.title: Mountain Pose (Tadasana): Instructions, Tips, Benefits & Videos

steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and down.
Lower your chin toward your chest, then slowly roll your head in a half circle until your ear is over one shoulder.
Roll back through the centre to the other shoulder, feeling a gentle stretch along the back and sides of your neck.
Breathe slowly and keep the movement smooth; each shoulder-to-shoulder pass counts as one rep.
Keep the arc in front of you rather than rolling your head far back, and stop if you feel dizzy or have pain.
george:neck-half-circles.note: Web search limit was reached before a source could be verified.

steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and your chin level, looking straight ahead.
Slowly turn your head to look over one shoulder until you feel a gentle stretch along the opposite side and back of your neck.
For a little more, rest your fingertips on your chin and ease it slightly further, keeping your shoulders square.
Breathe slowly, hold 15–30 seconds, return to centre and repeat to the other side.
Keep your chin level rather than tipping it up or down, and stop if you feel dizziness, tingling or sharp pain.
george:neck-rotation-stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out); standard movement, steps written from general knowledge.

steps: From hands and knees, bring one knee forward to just behind or slightly outside the same wrist and let the shin angle across the mat so the foot rests near the opposite hip.
Slide the other leg straight back, top of the foot on the mat, and turn both hips to face forward; put a folded blanket or block under the front hip if it doesn't reach the floor.
Breathe in and lengthen your spine; breathing out, walk your hands forward and lower onto your forearms or a block – or stay up on your hands for a gentler version.
Feel it in the outer hip and glute of the front leg and the front of the back hip; hold 5–10 slow breaths (30–60 seconds), then press back to hands and knees and switch sides.
Don't sink onto the front-leg hip or force the shin parallel to the front of the mat; if the front knee hurts, bring the foot closer to your body or do Figure Four on your back instead.

references.title: How to (Comfortably) Come Into Pigeon Pose
Pigeon Pose

steps: From hands and knees, place your hands under your shoulders and step your feet back so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Spread your fingers, press the floor away and draw your belly in so your hips neither sag nor pike up.
Reach back through your heels and forward through the crown of your head, looking at the floor just ahead of your hands.
Feel your core, shoulders and thighs working; breathe steadily and hold for 20–60 seconds.
For an easier version lower your knees to the mat, keeping a straight line from knees to head.
george:plank-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Sit on a chair and cross one foot over the opposite knee.
Hold your toes and gently pull them back toward your shin until you feel a stretch along the arch of your foot.
Keep the toes pulled back and slowly rub along the arch with the thumb of your other hand.
Breathe and hold 15–30 seconds, then switch feet.
Pull gently rather than forcing it; this works well first thing in the morning, before your first steps of the day.
george:plantar-fascia-toe-stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out); standard plantar fascia stretch.

steps: Lie on your back with a folded blanket under your shoulders, head on the mat and arms by your sides, palms down.
Press into your arms and use your core to lift your legs and hips up and over, lowering your toes toward the floor behind your head.
Support your back with your hands or interlace your fingers on the floor, keeping your weight on your shoulders rather than your neck.
Feel the stretch in your back, hamstrings and the back of your shoulders; breathe slowly and hold for 30 seconds to a minute.
Rest your feet on a chair if they don't reach the floor, never turn your head while up, and roll down slowly; skip it if you have neck problems.
george:plow-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Sit or stand tall and press your palms together in front of your chest, fingers pointing up and elbows out to the sides.
Keeping your palms pressed together, slowly lower your hands toward your waist until you feel a stretch in your wrists and the underside of your forearms.
Hold 15–30 seconds with relaxed breathing, then turn the backs of your hands together, fingers pointing down, and slowly lift them for the reverse stretch.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and the heels of your hands together, and ease off if you feel tingling or wrist pain.
george:prayer-wrist-stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out); standard wrist stretch.

steps: Lie face down with your forehead on your hands, bend both knees to 90 degrees and keep your knees together.
Slowly let both feet fall outward, away from each other, so your thighs rotate inward.
Keep your hips pressed into the floor and stop when you feel a stretch around the hips and buttocks, not in the knees.
Breathe slowly, hold 20–30 seconds, then bring your feet back to centre with control.
If your knees complain, let the knees sit slightly apart or lower one foot at a time.
george:prone-hip-internal-rotation-stret.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out).

steps: Lie face down and stretch one arm straight out to the side at shoulder height, palm down.
Place your other hand beside your chest and push into the floor to roll your body away from the outstretched arm.
Bend your top knee and plant that foot behind you for balance as you feel the stretch across your chest and the front of your shoulder.
Breathe slowly, hold 20–30 seconds, then roll back and switch sides.
Roll only as far as is comfortable with your neck relaxed, and bend the outstretched elbow to 90 degrees if the shoulder pinches.
george:prone-pec-stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out).

steps: Lie face down with your forehead on a folded towel, legs relaxed and arms reaching overhead with thumbs up, hands hovering just off the floor.
Sweep your arms out to the sides and down toward your hips, turning your palms up as your hands move behind your back.
Feel the muscles between and below your shoulder blades working, then reverse the path back overhead.
Breathe steadily and move slowly for the set reps, keeping your hands off the floor and your neck long.
Shorten the range or let your hands touch down if your shoulders pinch or cramp.
george:prone-swimmers.note: Web search limit was reached before a source could be verified.

steps: Start on hands and knees with your hips over your knees and hands under your shoulders.
Walk your hands forward and lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your hips high above your knees.
Rest your forehead or chin on the mat and press your palms down while drawing your hips back to lengthen your spine.
Feel the stretch in your shoulders, armpits and upper back; breathe into your upper back and hold for 30 seconds to a minute.
Don't sink so far that your lower back pinches; pad your knees or forehead with a blanket, then walk your hands back to come out.
george:puppy-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Stand with one foot about three feet (a metre) in front of the other, back foot turned out about 45 degrees and hips facing the front.
Keep both legs straight, inhale to lengthen your spine, then exhale and hinge from your hips over the front leg, hands on blocks or your shin.
Press evenly through both feet and draw the front hip back so your hips stay level.
Feel a strong stretch along the back of the front leg; breathe steadily for 5–8 breaths, then rise with a long spine and switch sides.
Keep your back flat instead of rounding to reach lower, and shorten your stance or slightly bend the front knee if the hamstring strains.
george:pyramid-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips, then sit your hips back a little toward your heels.
Place one hand behind your head with the elbow pointing out to the side.
Rotate that elbow down toward the opposite wrist, then turn it up toward the ceiling as far as you can while your hips stay still; feel your mid-back rotating.
Exhale as you turn up and follow the elbow with your eyes; do the set reps, then switch sides.
Do not twist from your lower back or shift your hips; a smaller rotation done well is better.
george:quadruped-thoracic-rotation.note: Web search limit was reached before a source could be verified.

steps: Kneel on hands and knees with hands under your shoulders, fingers spread and pointing forward.
Slowly rock your body forward over your hands and back again, feeling a stretch on the palm side of your wrists and forearms.
Then turn your hands so the fingers point toward your knees and rock back gently, and finally rest on the backs of your hands to stretch the top of the forearms.
Breathe steadily and do the set reps in each hand position.
Keep the pressure light and move only in a comfortable range; shift your hips back to take weight off your hands.
george:quadruped-wrist-rocks.note: Web search limit was reached before a source could be verified.

steps: Sit with your forearm resting on a table or thigh, elbow bent 90 degrees at your side, holding a tennis racket by the handle pointing straight up.
Slowly turn your palm down until the racket is horizontal, then rotate back through vertical and over to palm up.
You should feel your forearm muscles working to control the racket while your elbow and upper arm stay still.
Breathe steadily and move slowly for the set reps, then switch arms.
Grip higher up toward the racket head to make it easier, or hold nearer the end of the handle to add load.
george:racket-forearm-rotations.note: Standard pronation/supination drill, usually shown with a hammer or light dumbbell; web search limit was reached before a source could be verified.

steps: Lie on your back, bring the soles of your feet together and let your knees fall open to the sides.
Slide cushions or blocks under each thigh so the stretch in your groin stays mild; a bolster lengthwise under your back is optional.
Rest your arms by your sides with palms up, or place one hand on your belly and one on your chest.
Feel a gentle stretch in your inner thighs and groin; breathe slowly and stay for 1–5 minutes.
Don't push your knees down; to come out, use your hands to bring your knees together, then roll onto your side.
george:reclined-bound-angle-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Lie on your back with both legs straight and loop a strap around the ball of one foot.
Raise that leg toward the ceiling, holding the strap in both hands, and keep the other leg long with its foot flexed.
Walk your hands up the strap to draw the leg toward you until the back of the thigh stretches, keeping both hips on the floor.
Breathe slowly and hold for 30 seconds to a minute, then switch legs.
Bend the bottom knee with the foot flat if your lower back lifts, and hold the big toe instead only if your head and shoulders stay down.
george:reclined-hand-to-big-toe-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Sit in Hero Pose, on a block if needed, and place your hands on the floor behind you.
Lean back slowly onto your forearms, then onto a bolster or the floor only if your knees and lower back allow.
Keep your knees close together and on the floor, and lengthen your tailbone toward your knees so your lower back doesn't arch.
Feel the stretch along the front of your thighs, hips and ankles; breathe slowly and hold for 30 seconds to a few minutes.
Stop at the height where there's no knee or back pain; to come out, press up onto your forearms and hands before lifting your hips.

references.title: Reclining Hero Pose (Supta Virasana)
Everything You Need to Try Reclining Hero Pose (Supta Virasana)

george:reclined-hero-pose.note: Only for people who can sit comfortably in Hero Pose first.

steps: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat, then cross one ankle over the opposite knee and flex the crossed foot.
Lift the bottom foot off the floor and thread your hands behind that thigh or over the shin.
Draw the bottom thigh toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the outer hip and glute of the crossed leg.
Keep your head, shoulders and tailbone relaxed on the floor and breathe slowly for 30 seconds to a minute, then switch sides.
For a gentler stretch, keep the bottom foot on the floor or rest it against a wall.
george:reclined-pigeon-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose. The more common Sanskrit name for this figure-four is Sucirandhrasana; 'Supta Kapotasana' is used by some teachers.

steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and arms by your sides.
Step one foot back into a lunge and lower your back knee toward the floor while reaching both arms overhead.
Squeeze the glute of the back leg and lean slightly away from it to feel a stretch at the front of that hip, keeping your front knee over the ankle.
Inhale as you reach, then exhale as you push through your front foot to stand; alternate legs for the set reps.
Keep your ribs down rather than arching your lower back, and hold a wall or lunge less deeply if balance is hard.
george:reverse-lunge-with-overhead-reach.note: Web search limit was reached before a source could be verified.

steps: Stand or sit tall and bring your hands behind your back, backs of the hands together and fingers pointing down.
Turn your wrists so your fingers point up and slide your hands up toward your shoulder blades, pressing your palms together as far as is comfortable.
Roll your shoulders back and open your chest, drawing your elbows gently back.
Feel the stretch in your wrists, forearms and the front of your shoulders and chest; breathe evenly and hold for about 30 seconds.
If your palms won't meet, press fists together or hold opposite elbows behind your back, and stop if your wrists hurt.
george:reverse-prayer-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Sit with your knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, and place your hands behind your hips with fingers pointing toward your feet.
Press through your hands and feet to lift your hips until your thighs and torso are level, knees over ankles and wrists under shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes to hold your hips up and open across the front of your shoulders and chest, keeping your chin slightly tucked.
Feel your glutes, hamstrings and arms working and a stretch across your chest and shoulders; breathe steadily for about 5 breaths.
Don't let your hips sag or drop your head back if your neck is sensitive; lower gently and shake out your wrists between holds.
george:reverse-tabletop-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Start in Warrior II with your front knee bent over the ankle and your arms out at shoulder height.
Turn your front palm up, then reach that arm up and back over your head while your back hand slides lightly down the back leg.
Keep your front knee bent and hips low as you lengthen the whole front side of your body from hip to fingertips.
Feel the stretch along the side of your body and your front thigh working; breathe steadily for 3–5 breaths.
Don't lean your weight on the back hand or let the front knee straighten; return to Warrior II and switch sides.

references.title: Reverse Warrior Pose (Viparita Virabhadrasana) Instructions & Photos • Yoga Basics

steps: Stand with your feet together or hip-width apart, bend your knees and sit your hips back into Chair Pose.
Bring your palms together at the centre of your chest.
Exhale and turn to one side, hooking the opposite elbow outside that knee (left elbow past the right knee when turning right) and pressing your palms together.
Feel your thighs and glutes working and the twist through your middle back; breathe for 3–5 breaths, return to centre on an inhale and switch sides.
Keep your knees level so one doesn't slide ahead, and twist less with hands on your thighs if hooking the elbow strains your back.
george:revolved-chair-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: From Warrior III or a standing split, place the hand opposite your standing leg on a block or the floor directly under your shoulder.
Lift the back leg until it is level with your hip, foot flexed and toes pointing down, and keep both hips square to the floor.
Rotate your chest toward the standing-leg side and reach your other arm up, turning from your upper back rather than your lower back.
Feel your standing leg and hip working, a stretch in that hamstring and a twist through your middle back; hold for 3–5 steady breaths.
Keep the standing knee soft and look down if balancing is hard, or press the lifted foot into a wall; lower with control and switch sides.
george:revolved-half-moon-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Sit with one leg extended out to the side, then bend the other knee and rest that foot against the inner thigh of the straight leg.
Lean the side of your torso toward the straight leg, resting that forearm on the floor inside the leg or your hand on the shin.
Reach your top arm overhead toward the extended foot and turn your chest up toward the ceiling.
Feel the stretch along the top side of your body and in the straight leg's hamstring and inner thigh; breathe for 5–8 breaths, then switch sides.
Keep both sitting bones down; sit on a blanket or bend the straight knee slightly if your hamstring is tight, and avoid collapsing your chest.

references.title: Revolved Head-to-Knee Pose: How to Practice Parivrtta Janu Sirsasana
This Seated Yoga Pose Is the All-in-One Stretch You Need

steps: Step into a high lunge with your back heel lifted, front knee bent over the ankle and back leg straight.
Bring your palms together at your chest, then exhale and rotate toward the front leg, hooking the opposite elbow outside the front knee.
Press your palms together to help turn your chest to the side, keeping the back leg strong and your hips level.
Feel the twist through your middle back and your front thigh working; lengthen on each inhale and twist a little more on each exhale for 3–5 breaths.
Lower your back knee to the mat or rest your hands on blocks if balance is hard, then untwist and switch sides.

references.title: Back to Basics: Don’t Rush Revolved Crescent Lunge

steps: From Low Lunge with your back knee on a padded mat, place your hands on either side of your front foot, front knee over the ankle.
Keep the hand opposite your front leg on the floor or a block and reach the other arm toward the ceiling as you turn your chest toward the front leg.
Let your back hip sink forward slightly to keep a gentle stretch at the front of that hip.
Feel the twist through your upper and middle back; breathe slowly for about 5 breaths, lengthening on inhales and turning on exhales.
Twist from your upper back without forcing it and keep your gaze down if your neck is sensitive, then return to centre and switch sides.
george:revolved-low-lunge.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Step into a high lunge with your back heel lifted and front knee over the ankle, hands on either side of your front foot.
Place the hand opposite your front leg on the floor or a block outside the front foot, pressing that upper arm against the outer knee if you can.
Twist your chest toward the front leg and reach your top arm up toward the ceiling or alongside your ear.
Feel the twist through your middle back and your front thigh and glutes working; breathe steadily for 3–5 breaths, then switch sides.
Lengthen your spine before twisting deeper, and lower the back knee or use prayer hands with the elbow hooked if reaching the floor is too much.
george:revolved-side-angle-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Stand with your feet about a leg's length apart, front foot pointing forward, back foot turned out about 45 degrees and hips facing the front.
Hinge forward with a long spine and place the hand opposite your front leg on a block or the floor beside the front foot.
Rotate your chest toward the front leg and reach your other arm up, turning from your middle back rather than your neck.
Feel the stretch in the front leg's hamstring and the twist through your back; breathe steadily for 3–5 breaths, then switch sides.
Keep both legs straight but not locked and your hips level; use a higher block or shorten your stance if your back rounds.
george:revolved-triangle-pose.note: Not verified against a source: the shared web-search limit was reached before this entry, so references are empty; steps follow standard instruction for this pose.

steps: Stand with your feet about a leg's length apart and parallel, hinge forward from your hips and place your fingertips on the floor or a block under your shoulders.
Walk one hand to the centre, directly below your face, then inhale and sweep the other arm up toward the ceiling, turning your chest to that side.
Rotate from your ribcage and upper back rather than your lower back; you should feel the backs of your legs and the muscles along your spine stretching.
Breathe slowly for 3-6 breaths, lengthening your spine on each inhale and turning a little more on each exhale, then lower the arm and switch sides.
Bend your knees slightly or put the bottom hand on a block if your back rounds, and keep your weight even across both feet instead of sinking into one hip.

references.title: Lift Your Heels! The Little-Known Tip to Transform Your Practice
Practice These Twisting Yoga Poses to Stabilize Your Core

george:revolved-wide-legged-forward-fold.note: No dedicated pose page found; both references are articles/sequences that teach this twist as a variation of Wide-Legged Forward Bend.

steps: Sit tall and rest the fingertips of both hands on the collarbone of the side you want to stretch, gently holding it down.
Tilt your head away from that side, bringing the ear toward the opposite shoulder.
Then lift your chin slightly toward the ceiling until you feel a stretch along the front and side of your neck.
Breathe slowly, hold 15–30 seconds, bring your head back to centre and switch sides.
Keep the movement small and slow, and stop if you feel tingling, numbness or dizziness.
george:scalene-stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out). Changed 'turn chin up and away' to 'lift chin toward the ceiling', the common cue for the front scalene.

steps: Stand facing a wall and place the little-finger side of your forearms on it, elbows at shoulder height and about shoulder-width apart.
Gently press your forearms into the wall so your shoulder blades wrap forward; you should feel the muscles along the sides of your ribs switch on.
Slide your forearms up the wall into a Y as far as you can without shrugging, then lift them slightly off the wall for a second.
Return your forearms to the wall and slide back down slowly, exhaling on the way up; repeat for the set reps.
Do not let your shoulders creep toward your ears or your lower back arch; stop the slide where you start to shrug.
george:scapular-wall-slides.note: Web search limit was reached before a source could be verified.

steps: Sit tall on a chair or the floor with your legs extended or your heels resting lightly on the floor.
Pull your toes up toward your shins as far as is comfortable, feeling your calves lengthen.
Then point your toes away from you, feeling the front of your ankles stretch and your calves contract.
Keep a slow, steady rhythm through the full range and breathe normally; up and down together count as one rep.
Move only at the ankles without bending your knees, and work one foot at a time if that is easier to control.
george:seated-ankle-pumps.note: Web search limit was reached before a source could be verified.

steps: Sit near the front of a chair with your feet flat and hip-width apart and your hands resting on your knees.
Inhale, roll your pelvis forward, lift your chest and draw your shoulders back to arch your spine gently.
Exhale, roll your pelvis back, round your spine and let your chin drop toward your chest, feeling a stretch along your back.
Flow slowly between the two shapes with your breath for the set reps.
Move your whole spine rather than just your neck, and keep the arch small if your lower back is sensitive.

references.title: How to Do Cat-Cow Pose and Stretch the Muscles in Your Back

george:seated-cat-cow.note: Source covers the seated chair version as a modification of Cat-Cow.

steps: Sit near the front edge of a sturdy chair and stretch one leg forward with the heel on the floor and toes pointing up.
Keep your other foot flat, rest your hands on your thighs and sit up tall.
Hinge forward from your hips with a flat back until you feel a stretch behind the thigh and knee of the straight leg.
Breathe slowly, hold 20–30 seconds, then switch legs.
Don't round your back to reach lower; a small lean with a long spine is enough.
george:seated-chair-hamstring-stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out).

steps: Sit tall on a sturdy chair or bench with both feet flat, then cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Let the crossed knee relax toward the floor and keep that foot flexed to protect the knee.
Hinge forward from your hips with a long back until you feel a stretch deep in the buttock and outer hip of the crossed leg.
Breathe slowly, hold 20–30 seconds, then switch legs.
Don't push down hard on the knee or round your back; if you're tight, simply sitting upright may be enough.

references.title: How to Stretch Glutes: 7 Ways to Ease Tightness and Tension

steps: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat, and place your hands on the floor behind you, fingers pointing back away from your body.
Keeping your arms straight, slowly slide your hips forward, away from your hands, until you feel a stretch in the front of your arms and shoulders.
Lift your chest and draw your shoulders down away from your ears instead of letting them hunch.
Breathe slowly and hold 20–30 seconds.
Ease off if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder, and keep the elbows straight but not locked.
george:seated-floor-biceps-stretch.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out).

steps: Sit with your legs straight out in front of you and your feet flexed, on a folded blanket if your lower back rounds when you sit upright.
Inhale to sit tall, then exhale and hinge forward from your hips, sliding your hands along your legs to your shins, ankles or feet.
Lead with your chest toward your toes rather than your head toward your knees; you should feel the stretch in the middle of the backs of your thighs.
Hold for 1-3 minutes, lifting your chest slightly on each inhale and easing a little deeper on each exhale.
If you can't reach your feet, loop a strap around them or bend your knees, and stop folding when your back starts to round.

references.title: Seated Forward Bend: How to Practice Paschimottanasana
Master Paschimottanasana in 6 Steps

steps: Sit tall near the front of a sturdy chair with both feet flat on the floor.
Lift one knee and wrap your hands around the shin just below the knee.
Draw the knee toward your chest while keeping your back tall and shoulders relaxed, feeling a stretch in the buttock and lower back.
Breathe slowly, hold 20–30 seconds, then lower the foot and switch legs.
Don't slump to bring the knee closer; if holding the shin bothers your knee, hold behind the thigh instead.
george:seated-knee-hug.note: No reference verified (shared web-search budget ran out).

steps: Sit tall with your legs straight and a little wider than hip-width, feet flexed and arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Inhale and rotate your torso toward one leg, keeping both sitting bones on the mat.
Exhale and fold forward, reaching the opposite hand past the little-toe side of that foot while your back arm reaches behind you; feel the stretch in the hamstring and back.
Inhale to sit tall, return to the centre and alternate sides for the set reps.
Do not let your hips shift or lift; bend your knees slightly or sit on a cushion if your lower back rounds.
george:seated-saw.note: Classic Pilates Saw; web search limit was reached before a source could be verified.

steps: Sit tall in a sturdy chair whose firm backrest reaches about the bottom of your shoulder blades, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Lace your fingers lightly behind your head with your elbows pointing forward, supporting your head rather than pulling on it.
Lean your upper back over the top of the backrest, letting your elbows open toward the ceiling, until you feel your mid-back arch and your chest open.
Breathe out as you lean back and hold for a few slow breaths, then sit up and shift slightly higher or lower to work another spot.
Keep your ribs down and lower back still; the bend should come from between your shoulder blades, not from tipping your head or pushing your belly forward.

references.title: Exercises for Thoracic Outlet Syndrome
How to Crack Your Back: 10 Ways to Try, Video, and Tips

steps: Sit in a 90/90 position: front shin across your body, back leg bent out to the side behind you, both knees at about 90 degrees.
Sit tall, lean slightly over the front shin, then press the front knee and shin into the floor and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips up into a tall kneel.
You should feel your glutes and outer hips working and a stretch around the hips; breathe out as you rise.
Lower back down to the 90/90 with control, then swap your legs to the other side and repeat; do 5–8 reps per side.
If you tip backwards, put a hand on the floor or hold a bench for help rather than swinging up with momentum.

references.title: Unlock Tight Hips for Good With the Shin Box Stretch

george:shin-box-get-up.note: Only one reputable source found before the shared search budget ran out; it describes the get-up as rising from 90/90 toward the front foot into a kneel.

steps: Sit cross-legged, then slide one foot under the opposite knee toward the outside of that hip and stack the other knee on top, both feet beside your hips.
Sit evenly on both sitting bones, adding a blanket under your hips if one side lifts, and stay upright or walk your hands forward to fold.
You should feel a deep stretch in your outer hips and buttocks, never sharp pain in your knees.
Breathe slowly and stay for 1-3 minutes (up to 5 in a yin class), then press up, uncross your legs and switch which knee is on top.
If the stacked knees strain, put a folded blanket between them, sit higher, or straighten the bottom leg for Half Shoelace.

references.title: Shoelace pose - YogaEasy

steps: Stand tall (or kneel upright), make a firm fist with one hand, and squeeze your glutes and brace your core so your ribs and trunk stay still.
Raise the straight arm forward and up overhead as far as you can, thumb leading, then near the top turn the palm to face outward.
Keep tracing the biggest circle you can, back and down behind you, finishing at your side with the palm facing back; you should feel effort all around the shoulder.
Take 10–20 seconds per circle and breathe steadily; do 3–5 slow reps, then reverse the direction and switch arms.
Don't lean, twist or arch your back to get the arm higher; a smaller circle with a still body is the goal.

references.title: 3 Great Ways to Improve Your Shoulder Mobility (Not Stability)

george:shoulder-cars.note: The source shows the drill in tall kneeling; standing works the same way. No Healthline/NASM/ACE page for CARs turned up.

steps: Stand beside a table or counter, rest your other hand on it and bend forward at the hips so the working arm hangs straight down, fully relaxed.
Gently rock your body so the hanging arm swings in small circles, letting momentum move it rather than the shoulder muscles.
You should feel the shoulder joint loosen and ease, not pain; you can also swing forward-back and side to side.
Breathe normally and do about 10 circles in each direction, then switch arms if both need it.
If you notice yourself lifting the arm with effort, make the swings smaller and let your body do the moving.

references.title: 3 Frozen Shoulder Exercises to Relieve Pain
Shoulder exercises - Mayo Clinic

steps: Squat on the balls of your feet with your knees together, then twist to one side and place both hands shoulder-width apart on the mat beside the outside of one thigh.
Bend your elbows straight back to make a shelf and rest your outer thigh on the upper arm that crosses your body, keeping your knees pressed together.
Lean forward into your hands until your feet float and your hips stay high; you'll feel your obliques, triceps and shoulders working hard.
Breathe steadily for 3-5 breaths, then lower your feet with control and repeat on the other side.
Rest your forehead on a block or cushion while learning, spread your fingers wide, and practise on a firm floor, never a soft surface.

references.title: Side Crow and Side Crane Pose: How to Practice Parsva Bakasana
Challenge Pose: 4 Steps To Side Crow (Parsva Bakasana)

steps: Stand in a wide straddle, about a leg's length between your feet, with your toes turned slightly out.
Bend one knee deeply and sit your hips back toward that heel, keeping the other leg straight and turning its toes up to the ceiling.
You should feel a stretch along the inner thigh and back of the straight leg, while the bent leg's thigh and glute work.
Keep your chest lifted with your hands on the floor or pressed together at your chest, breathe for 5-8 breaths, then shift through the centre to the other side.
If your bent heel lifts, keep your hands down for support or rest the heel on a folded mat, and only sink as low as your hips allow.

references.title: Side Lunge
Working Toward the Splits? These Stretches Will Help.

steps: Start in Plank Pose, then shift onto one hand and roll onto the outer edge of that side's foot, stacking the other foot on top.
Press the floor away with your bottom hand under your shoulder, lift your hips so your body forms one line from head to heels, and reach your top arm up.
You should feel your side abs, the supporting shoulder and the outer hip of the bottom leg working.
Breathe steadily for 3-5 breaths or 15-30 seconds, then return to Plank and switch sides.
Don't let your hips sag or rock back; for an easier version, lower your bottom knee to the mat or stagger your feet.

references.title: Side Plank Pose: How to Practice Vasisthasana
Your Step-by-Step Guide to Come Into Side Plank (Vasisthasana)

steps: Lie on the side to stretch, head on a pillow, that arm straight out in front at shoulder height and the elbow bent to 90 degrees, fingers up.
Roll your body back about 20–30 degrees so your shoulder blade isn't trapped under you.
With your other hand, gently press the forearm down toward the floor until you feel a stretch at the back of the shoulder.
Breathe slowly and hold for about 30 seconds, then ease the pressure off before resting.
Keep the pressure light and stop if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder or pain in the joint.
george:sleeper-stretch.note: Steps describe the modified sleeper stretch (rolled back 20–30 degrees); the classic version lies straight on the shoulder. No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Lie face down with your legs hip-width apart, then prop yourself up on your forearms with your elbows under or slightly ahead of your shoulders.
Press your forearms down and draw your chest forward and up, sliding your shoulders away from your ears and keeping your neck long.
You should feel a gentle arch in your lower back and a mild stretch across your chest and belly; let your glutes stay relaxed.
Breathe slowly for 5-10 breaths or up to a few minutes, then lower your chest and rest your head on your hands.
If your lower back pinches, walk your elbows further forward to lower your chest, and avoid shrugging your shoulders up.

references.title: Sphinx Pose (Salamba Bhujangasana) Instructions & Photos • Yoga Basics

steps: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart, bend forward and grab under your toes, bending your knees as much as you need.
Keeping hold of your toes, drop your hips into a deep squat with your chest lifted and your elbows inside your knees, gently pushing them apart.
Raise one arm and then the other overhead to lift your chest, then return your hands to your toes.
Lift your hips and straighten your legs as far as is comfortable to feel your hamstrings, then stand tall; breathe steadily and do 8–10 slow reps.
If you can't reach your toes, hold your shins, and keep your heels on the floor instead of rolling onto your toes.

references.title: Relieve Tight Hips With the Deep Squat to Hamstring Stretch
8 Mobility Exercises and Stretches to Improve Your Clean and Front Squat

steps: Sit on a stability ball, then slowly walk your feet forward until your lower and middle back rest on the ball.
Lean back so the ball supports your spine and head, and let your arms open out to the sides or reach overhead.
Keep your feet wide and planted for balance and feel the stretch across your chest, abdomen and the fronts of your hips.
Breathe deeply and hold for 20–30 seconds, or gently roll a little forward and back to vary the spot.
To come out, tuck your chin, bring your hands to your thighs and walk your feet back in; keep your arms by your sides if overhead feels too intense.
george:stability-ball-backbend.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Kneel on the floor beside a stability ball and drape the side of your torso over it, with your hip resting against the ball.
Extend your top leg out long with its foot on the floor and keep your bottom knee down for support.
Reach your top arm overhead and let your body curve over the ball until you feel a stretch from your hip to your fingertips.
Breathe slowly into the stretched side and hold for 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.
Keep your chest facing forward rather than rolling toward the floor; leave the top hand on your hip for an easier version.
george:stability-ball-side-stretch.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Sit with your legs straight out in front of you, big toes together or close and feet flexed so your toes point up.
Place your hands on the floor beside your hips, fingers forward, and press down to lift your chest, stacking your shoulders over your hips.
Firm your thighs and press the backs of your legs toward the floor; you'll feel your core and back working and a light stretch behind your legs.
Breathe evenly for 5-10 breaths, keeping your chin level and your shoulders relaxed.
If your lower back rounds, sit on a folded blanket so your hips are higher than your knees, or rest your knees on a rolled blanket.

references.title: Staff Pose: How to Practice Dandasana
Master Dandasana in 6 Steps

steps: Stand with your feet about twice shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward or slightly out.
Bend one knee and shift your hips toward that side, keeping the other leg straight with its foot flat.
Rest your hands on the bent thigh and keep your chest up until you feel a stretch along the inner thigh of the straight leg.
Breathe steadily and hold for 20–30 seconds, then shift across to the other side.
Keep the bent knee tracking over your toes; if balance is tricky, use a narrower stance or hold a chair.
george:standing-adductor-stretch.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and place your palms on your lower back, fingers pointing down.
Inhale to lift your chest and draw your elbows toward each other, then exhale and lean back gently as you press your hips slightly forward.
You should feel a stretch across your chest, belly and the fronts of your hips, not compression in your lower back.
Hold for 3-5 breaths with your thighs and glutes lightly engaged, then come up on an inhale, lifting your head last.
Keep the bend small and your chin level instead of dropping your head back, and stop at any pinching in your lower back.

references.title: Standing Backbend Pose (Anuvittasana) Instructions & Photos • Yoga Basics

steps: Stand tall near a wall or chair, shift your weight onto one leg and cross the other ankle over the standing knee, flexing the lifted foot.
Bend the standing knee and sit your hips back as if lowering into a chair, keeping your chest long.
You should feel the stretch in the outer hip and buttock of the crossed leg; hinge forward slightly from your hips to deepen it.
Bring your palms together at your chest or rest them on the crossed shin and hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing evenly, then stand up and switch sides.
Hold the wall or chair if you wobble, and don't let the standing knee cave inward.

references.title: How to Stretch Glutes: 7 Ways to Ease Tightness and Tension
10 Go-To Glute Stretches to Round Out Your Yoga Practice

steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your hips.
Soften your knees and hinge forward from your hips, letting your hands rest on the floor, blocks or your shins and your head hang.
Feel the stretch along the backs of your legs and through your back; bend your knees enough to rest your belly on your thighs if you're tight.
Breathe slowly for 30-60 seconds, easing a little deeper on each exhale, then bend your knees and roll up slowly.
Avoid locking your knees or forcing straight legs, and keep the knees well bent if you have back problems.

references.title: Standing Forward Bend: How to Practice Uttanasana
Standing Forward Fold (Uttanasana): Instructions, Tips & Benefits

steps: Stand side-on to a wall, about a forearm's length away, with your near hand or forearm resting on it for balance.
Cross the leg nearest the wall behind your other leg, keeping both feet flat.
Push that hip out toward the wall while leaning your upper body slightly away, until you feel a stretch along the outside of the hip and thigh.
For more stretch, raise the wall-side arm overhead toward the other side; breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds, then turn around to switch.
Keep your chest facing forward rather than twisting, and don't slump your weight into the wall.
george:standing-outer-hip-stretch.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand with your feet hip- to shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent and hands on your hips.
Slowly push your hips forward, then to one side, back and to the other side, drawing one big, smooth circle.
Keep your head and shoulders roughly over your feet so the motion comes from your pelvis; you should feel your lower back and hips loosen.
Breathe normally and do 8–10 circles in one direction, then the same number the other way.
Start with small circles and widen them as you loosen up; don't force the range if your lower back pinches.

references.title: Try This: 24 Standing Ab Exercises to Strengthen and Define Your Core

george:standing-pelvic-circles.note: Source lists it as standing hip circles (hands on hips, feet planted).

steps: Stand tall next to a wall or chair and hold it with one hand for balance.
Bend the knee of your outside leg and take hold of that ankle or foot with your free hand, drawing the heel toward your buttock.
Keep your knees side by side and gently tuck your tailbone until you feel the stretch along the front of your thigh.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds, then turn around and switch legs.
Avoid arching your lower back or letting the knee drift out to the side; loop a towel around your ankle if you can't reach it.
george:standing-quad-stretch.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, knees soft and arms relaxed by your sides.
Tuck your chin toward your chest and slowly roll down one vertebra at a time, letting your head and arms hang as your hands travel toward the floor.
Pause at the bottom and breathe into your back; you should feel a stretch along your spine and the backs of your legs.
Roll back up slowly from the base of your spine, stacking each vertebra with your head coming up last; do 5–8 reps.
Bend your knees more if your lower back or hamstrings strain, and come up slowly if you feel light-headed.
george:standing-roll-down.note: Not source-verified: the shared web-search budget ran out (only a seated Pilates roll-down page was found). Steps follow standard Pilates instruction.

steps: Stand tall holding a wall or rail for balance.
Place the top of one foot on the floor slightly behind you, toes pointed back so the laces side rests on the floor.
Gently bend your standing knee and press the ankle forward until you feel a stretch along the front of your shin and top of the ankle.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds, starting with light pressure and building gradually, then switch feet.
Keep most of your weight on the standing leg; if your foot cramps, try it seated with the foot tucked back beside the chair.
george:standing-shin-stretch.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: From a Standing Forward Fold, place your fingertips on the floor or on blocks a little in front of your feet.
Shift your weight into one foot and lift the other leg straight up behind you, toes pointing down and hips kept square to the floor.
You should feel a strong stretch in the hamstring and calf of the standing leg, with the glute of the lifted leg working.
Breathe steadily for 30 seconds to 1 minute, then lower the leg with control and switch sides.
Don't chase height by twisting the hip open; keep the standing kneecap facing forward and soften that knee if your hamstrings pull.

references.title: Standing Split (Urdhva Prasarita Eka Padasana)
Standing Split (Urdhva Prasarita Eka Padasana) Cues

steps: Stand tall and hold one arm straight out in front of you at shoulder height, palm facing down.
With your other hand, gently bend the wrist down, drawing the back of the hand toward you.
Keep the elbow straight and feel the stretch along the top of your forearm; making a loose fist first adds more stretch.
Breathe slowly and hold for 15–30 seconds, then switch arms.
Use gentle pressure only and ease off if you feel tingling or elbow pain; bending the elbow slightly makes it easier.
george:standing-wrist-extensor-stretch.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand tall and hold one arm straight out in front of you at shoulder height, palm facing up.
With your other hand, gently pull the fingers down and back toward you.
Keep the elbow straight and feel the stretch along the inside of your forearm and palm.
Breathe slowly and hold for 15–30 seconds, then switch arms.
Pull gently rather than cranking the fingers back; bend the elbow slightly for an easier stretch.
george:standing-wrist-flexor-stretch.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: From Mountain Pose, step your feet wide so your ankles sit roughly under your wrists when your arms are out to the sides, toes facing forward.
Raise your arms to shoulder height, palms down, and reach actively through your fingertips, your feet and the crown of your head.
You'll feel your legs, shoulders and core working as you stretch out in all five directions.
Breathe steadily for 4-8 breaths, then lower your arms and step your feet back together.
Keep your knees soft rather than locked and your ribs drawn in; narrow your stance or rest your hands on your hips if balance or shoulders are a problem.

references.title: Five Pointed Star Pose (Utthita Tadasana) • Yoga Basics

steps: Stand on the edge of a step with the balls of both feet on it and your heels hanging off, holding a rail for balance.
Slowly let one or both heels sink below the step until you feel a stretch in your calves.
Hold with your knees straight for the upper calf, then soften the knees slightly to shift the stretch toward the lower calf and Achilles.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds in each position.
Lower gradually without bouncing, and start with both feet sharing the load before trying one leg at a time.
george:step-heel-drop-calf-stretch.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand in Mountain Pose, inhale and sweep your arms overhead, then exhale and fold forward.
Inhale to a half lift with a flat back, then exhale, step back to Plank and lower all the way down, knees down if needed.
Inhale into Cobra or Upward-Facing Dog, then exhale back to Downward-Facing Dog for five breaths, feeling the stretch through your hamstrings, calves and shoulders.
Step or walk your feet to your hands, inhale to a half lift, exhale to fold, then inhale to rise with arms overhead and exhale to Mountain Pose.
Link one breath to each movement; if your wrists or shoulders tire, lower on your knees or skip the lowering and go from Plank straight to Downward Dog.

references.title: Surya Namaskar A: How to Flow Through Sun Salutations - Yoga Journal
Sun Salutations: A Complete Guide to Surya Namaskar A

steps: From Mountain Pose, inhale and bend your knees into Chair Pose with your arms overhead, then exhale and fold forward.
Inhale to a half lift, then exhale, step back and lower through Four-Limbed Staff Pose, inhale to Upward-Facing Dog and exhale to Downward-Facing Dog.
Inhale and step your right foot forward into Warrior I, then flow through Plank, lowering, Upward Dog and Downward Dog again; repeat with the left foot forward.
Hold Downward-Facing Dog for five breaths, then step forward, half lift, fold, and inhale back into Chair Pose before standing in Mountain Pose.
Your thighs and shoulders work hardest here; lower on your knees or swap Upward Dog for Cobra if needed, and keep one breath per movement.

references.title: Everything You Need to Know About Sun Salutations in Yoga
A Guide to Hacking Your Sun Salutations - Yoga Journal

george:sun-salutation-b.note: References are general Sun Salutation guides that cover the B sequence rather than dedicated B pages; which foot steps forward first varies by teacher.

steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, holding a dowel or broomstick at shoulder width with arms straight above your chest.
Slowly lower the dowel overhead toward the floor behind you, keeping your elbows straight.
Stop when you feel a stretch along the sides of your back and under your arms.
Breathe slowly and hold at a comfortable edge for 20–30 seconds, then bring the dowel back over your chest.
Keep your lower ribs and lower back gently heavy on the floor instead of arching to find extra range.
george:supine-dowel-overhead-stretch.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, one elbow bent to 90 degrees and tucked against your side, holding one end of a dowel or racket.
Hold the other end with your free hand and use it to gently push the working forearm out and away from your body.
Keep the elbow pinned to your side and stop at a mild stretch at the front of the shoulder.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds, then switch arms.
Put a small folded towel under the elbow for comfort; to progress, move the elbow slightly away from your side, staying below shoulder height.
george:supine-external-rotation-stretch.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Lie on your back, hug one knee into your chest and stretch the other leg long on the floor.
Use the opposite hand to guide the bent knee across your body toward the floor, and stretch your other arm out to the side at shoulder height.
Keep both shoulder blades heavy and turn your head away from the knee if your neck allows; you should feel the stretch in your lower back, outer hip and chest.
Breathe slowly into your belly for 1-2 minutes, then bring the knee back to centre and switch sides.
If the knee doesn't reach the floor or your shoulder lifts, rest the knee on a folded blanket or pillow instead of forcing it down.

references.title: Here's Why A Spinal Twist May Help Relieve Your Low Back Pain

george:supine-spinal-twist.note: Reference is an article on the pose rather than a step-by-step pose page; it shows the both-knees version, while these steps use the common one-knee version.

steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, and a yoga block within reach.
Press into your feet to lift your hips, slide the block under your sacrum (the flat bone at the base of your spine) and lower your weight onto it.
Rest your arms by your sides, palms up; you should feel a gentle stretch across the fronts of your hips and chest, not pressure in your lower back.
Breathe slowly and stay for 1-5 minutes, then lift your hips, remove the block and lower your back to the floor.
Start with the block on its lowest height and keep it off your lower back; add a folded blanket on top if it feels hard.

references.title: How to Use Props in Bridge Pose to Improve Your Alignment
Take a Load Off: 5 Supported Yoga Poses for When Your Body Needs a Break.

steps: Fold two or three blankets into a firm stack and lie with your shoulders on its edge, head on the floor, knees bent and arms by your sides.
Press your arms down, swing your knees toward your face to lift your hips, then bend your elbows and support your back with your hands.
Walk your hands toward your shoulder blades and straighten your legs toward the ceiling, keeping your weight on your shoulders and upper arms, never your neck.
Breathe steadily for 30 seconds to a few minutes, then bend your knees and roll down slowly one vertebra at a time.
Never turn your head while up; if you have neck problems, high blood pressure or are new to inversions, do Legs-Up-the-Wall instead.
george:supported-shoulder-stand.note: Not web-verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps follow standard teaching of the pose and still need 1-2 references.

steps: Come onto your hands and knees with your wrists under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, hip-width apart.
Spread your fingers and press evenly through your whole hand, then lengthen your spine so your back is flat from tailbone to the crown of your head.
Draw your belly in lightly; you'll feel your core and shoulders working gently to hold a level back.
Breathe steadily for 5-10 breaths, keeping your gaze down at the mat just ahead of your hands.
Don't let your lower back sag or your shoulders sink toward the floor, and put a folded blanket under your knees if they're sensitive.
george:tabletop-pose.note: Not web-verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps follow standard teaching of the pose and still need 1-2 references.

steps: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent to about 90 degrees, head on a pillow, and both arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, palms together.
Keep your knees stacked on the floor, then as you breathe out, lift the top arm up and over, opening your chest toward the ceiling like a book.
Follow your hand with your eyes and let the arm settle toward the floor behind you; feel the stretch across your chest and the turn in your upper back.
Pause for a breath, bring the arm back over slowly, and do 8–10 reps before switching sides.
If your top knee lifts, the twist is coming from your lower back; hold the knee down with your bottom hand or a cushion.
george:thoracic-open-book.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out before this entry. Current steps were already correct.

steps: Start on your hands and knees with your wrists under your shoulders and your hips over your knees.
Inhale and reach one arm up to open your chest, then exhale and slide that arm under your chest, palm up, until that shoulder and ear rest on the mat.
Keep your hips stacked over your knees; you should feel the stretch across the back of that shoulder and through your upper back.
Rest your other hand on the floor or reach it overhead, breathe slowly for 30-60 seconds, then press back up and switch sides.
Don't load your neck; if it's uncomfortable, rest your head on a folded blanket or thread the arm less far.
george:thread-the-needle.note: Not web-verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps follow standard teaching of the pose and still need 1-2 references.

steps: Start in Downward-Facing Dog with your hands shoulder-width apart and your feet hip-width apart.
Inhale and lift one leg straight up behind you, reaching back through the heel while both hips stay level and face the floor.
Press evenly through both hands and the standing heel; you'll feel the standing leg's hamstring and calf stretch and your shoulders and core working.
Hold for 3-5 breaths, then lower the leg on an exhale and switch sides.
Don't trade level hips for a higher leg; for a hip opener, bend the lifted knee and let that hip open toward the ceiling.
george:three-legged-dog.note: Not web-verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps follow standard teaching of the pose and still need 1-2 references.

steps: Face a wall and place the ball of one foot against it, heel on the floor and that leg straight.
Keep your other foot a step behind and rest your hands on the wall.
Gently lean your hips toward the wall until you feel a deep stretch through the calf and the arch of the foot.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds, then bend the front knee slightly to shift the stretch toward the Achilles before switching sides.
Keep the heel down and hips facing the wall; set the toes lower on the wall if it feels too intense.
george:toes-up-wall-calf-stretch.note: No reference verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry; steps written from standard practice and the existing description.

steps: Stand tall, hold a towel in one hand and drape it over that shoulder, then reach your other hand behind your lower back and grab the hanging end.
Gently pull the towel upward with the top hand so the lower hand slides up your spine as far as is comfortable.
Feel a stretch in the front and top of the lower shoulder; the top arm may also feel a stretch along the back of the upper arm.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds, then switch which hand is on top.
Keep your shoulders level and chest lifted, and ease off right away if you feel pinching or pain in the joint.

references.title: Frozen Shoulder Exercises from a Physical Therapist
4 Triceps Stretches for Tight Muscles

george:towel-shoulder-internal-rotation-.note: HSS describes a variant where you hold the towel horizontally and pull it up to the side. Healthline describes the vertical over-the-shoulder version used here.

steps: Stand tall with your arms reaching forward at shoulder height.
Walk forward, kicking one straight leg up in front of you to a comfortable height while reaching the opposite hand toward your toes.
Keep your chest up and the standing knee soft; you should feel a stretch along the back of the kicking leg.
Lower the leg, step through and repeat with the other leg; breathe steadily and do 8–10 kicks per leg.
Kick only as high as you can while keeping the leg straight and your back upright; don't round over to reach the foot.
george:toy-soldiers.note: Not source-verified: shared web-search budget ran out before this entry.

steps: Stand tall on one leg and place the sole of the other foot on your inner ankle, calf or upper thigh, never against the side of the knee.
Press the foot and standing leg firmly into each other, keep your hips level and let the bent knee open out to the side.
You'll feel the standing foot, ankle and glute working to balance, plus a gentle stretch in the inner thigh of the bent leg.
Bring your palms together at your chest or reach overhead, fix your gaze on a still point and breathe steadily for 30-60 seconds before switching sides.
If you wobble, keep your toes on the floor with the heel against your ankle, or rest one hand on a wall.
george:tree-pose.note: Not web-verified: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry could be searched; steps follow standard teaching of the pose and still need 1-2 references.

steps: Stand with your feet about a leg's length apart, front foot pointing to the front of the mat and back foot turned slightly in, both legs straight but not locked.
Reach your front arm forward over your front leg, then tilt your torso down and rest that hand on your shin, a block or the floor.
Extend your top arm toward the ceiling and open your chest; feel the stretch in the front leg's hamstring, your inner thighs and along the side of your waist.
Breathe for 5-8 breaths, then press through your feet to rise with control and switch sides.

steps: Sit sideways with one hip against a wall, then lie back and swing your legs up the wall, keeping your buttocks close to it.

steps: Start in Downward-Facing Dog and lift into Three-Legged Dog, then bend the lifted knee and open that hip toward the ceiling.
